methods_detailed.name: onUpdate
methods_detailed.detail_long: onUpdate runs every client tick for the local player and first gates on worldObj.isBlockLoaded at BlockPos(posX, 0, posZ) so no packets are sent from unloaded areas. It calls super.onUpdate first to run entity physics, collision, and position integration before any networking decision. If isRiding is true it takes the vehicle branch and does not call onUpdateWalkingPlayer at all. In the riding branch it queues a C03 C05PacketPlayerLook with current rotationYaw, rotationPitch and onGround every tick because the server drives vehicle position. It also queues a C0CPacketInput with moveStrafing, moveForward, movementInput.jump and movementInput.sneak so the server can steer the ridden horse, boat, pig or minecart. If not riding it delegates to onUpdateWalkingPlayer which owns the on-foot C03 family and C0B throttling. This split prevents double-sending position while riding and explains why ground-spoof and blink cheats hook the on-foot path. The receiver NetHandlerPlayServer validates look and input and applies them to the riding entity rather than the player.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The isBlockLoaded guard stops updates when the player column is unloaded, preventing desync packets from void or unloaded chunks. super.onUpdate runs shared EntityLivingBase physics before networking so sent values reflect the new tick. The isRiding branch constructs C05PacketPlayerLook from live yaw, pitch and onGround, telling the server where the rider looks while the vehicle moves. The next line constructs C0CPacketInput from strafe, forward, jump and sneak, which is the only channel for steering ridden entities. The else calls onUpdateWalkingPlayer for the on-foot C03 and C0B logic, so suppressing either queue call creates a blink-like stall that the server later corrects.

methods_detailed.name: onUpdateWalkingPlayer
methods_detailed.detail_long: onUpdateWalkingPlayer compares live isSprinting against cached serverSprintState and live isSneaking against serverSneakState, sending C0BPacketEntityAction START or STOP only on a flip to save bandwidth. It then gates all position traffic on isCurrentViewEntity so only the camera entity transmits, ignoring other render-view switches. It computes d0, d1 from posX and boundingBox.minY minus lastReported, d2 from posZ, and d3, d4 from yaw and pitch deltas. It sets flag2 when squared positional delta exceeds 9.0E-4D or positionUpdateTicks reaches 20, forcing a keep-alive at least once per second. It sets flag3 when yaw or pitch changed at all, then picks C06 pos-look when both moved, C04 position when only moved, C05 look when only rotated, else bare C03 onGround keep-alive. When ridingEntity is non-null it sends a special C06 with motionX, -999.0D Y and motionZ as a stall marker and forces flag2 false. Finally it increments positionUpdateTicks, and on flag2 or flag3 copies current pos and angles into lastReported fields and zeroes the tick counter, which is the state blink freezes.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The d0 through d4 lines snapshot how far position and look drifted since the last transmitted report, using boundingBox.minY for the feet Y the server validates. flag2 applies the 9.0E-4D squared-distance threshold plus the 20-tick forced update, which is why standing still still sends a bare C03 once per second. flag3 fires on any yaw or pitch delta, separating look-only C05 traffic from movement. The four-way if chain maps the two booleans to C06, C04, C05 or base C03, each carrying the onGround boolean the server uses for fall damage, so spoofing that bit is ground-spoof. The riding branch with -999.0D Y signals the server not to apply on-foot movement, and freezing these queues while continuing to render locally is exactly a blink exploit.

methods_detailed.name: onLivingUpdate
methods_detailed.detail_long: onLivingUpdate runs before physics each tick and first decrements sprintingTicksLeft, sprintToggleTimer and timeUntilPortal so sprint expiry, double-tap windows and portal cooldowns age correctly. It handles double-tap-W sprint by setting sprintToggleTimer to 7 on first tap and calling setSprinting true on second tap within the window, gated on food above 6, allowFlying, onGround and not using an item or blinded. It handles the sprint key, sprint cancel on slowdown or collision, and slows movementInput by 0.2 while using an item. For flight it forces isFlying true in spectator mode with a C13 send, and detects double-space via flyToggleTimer 7 to toggle capabilities.isFlying and call sendPlayerAbilities which emits C13PacketPlayerAbilities. It manages horse jump charging with horseJumpPowerCounter from -10 through 10, sending C0B RIDING_JUMP on release and computing power up to 0.8 plus curve, plus horse inventory via C0B OPEN_INVENTORY. On landing while flying in non-spectator it clears isFlying and re-sends C13, and it accumulates timeInPortal toward 1.0 for dimension travel. The server NetHandlerPlayServer re-validates abilities and jump power, so forged C13 or C0B values are the classic fly and horse-jump cheat vectors.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The allowFlying outer gate ensures only creative or spectator clients can enter the toggle logic, otherwise no C13 is produced here. The spectator inner branch forces isFlying true and calls sendPlayerAbilities, which queues C13 with the full capabilities object for server approval. The double-space detector uses flyToggleTimer 7 ticks to distinguish a tap from a hold, flipping isFlying and re-sending C13 on the second press. The isFlying plus isCurrentViewEntity block then applies flySpeed vertical motion locally, so a forged C13 that enables flying without permission lets the client move vertically until the server corrects it.

methods_detailed.name: sendChatMessage
methods_detailed.detail_long: sendChatMessage takes the raw string from the chat GUI or command line with no client-side filtering, length splitting or command parsing. It wraps the string verbatim in a new C01PacketChatMessage and adds it to sendQueue via addToSendQueue for TCP flush. It does not distinguish slash commands from public chat, leaving that decision to NetHandlerPlayServer on the receiving side. The server then routes slash-prefixed text to the command dispatcher and other text to broadcast with spam and visibility checks. Because the client sends the full string, server plugins see the exact typed content including formatting codes. Dropping or mutating this packet silences the player, while flooding it is chat spam. No other packet is emitted here, so chat has no movement or inventory side effects.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The single addToSendQueue line shows the entire method body, constructing C01PacketChatMessage directly from the message argument with no rewrite. sendQueue is the NetHandlerPlayClient channel to the server, so the text leaves the client in one TCP packet. The neighboring swingItem and respawnPlayer snippets show the same one-line queue pattern for C0A and C16, confirming this class delegates all authority to the server. If this C01 is blocked the server never sees chat, and if forged at high rate the server throttle or kick applies.

methods_detailed.name: swingItem
methods_detailed.detail_long: swingItem first calls super.swingItem to run the client-side arm swing timer and render animation immediately without waiting for the server. It then constructs an empty C0APacketAnimation with no entity ID or hand argument, because 1.8.9 has a single swing type inferred from the sender. It queues that packet on sendQueue so the server and then other clients via S0B animation can mirror the motion. It is called for attacks, block hits and item use visuals, decoupling visual feedback from damage outcome. The server uses the C0A arrival time as a heuristic alongside C02 attack and C07 dig packets for anti-cheat timing. Suppressing C0A while still attacking creates silent swings that look like no-animation kill-aura. The receiver NetHandlerPlayServer broadcasts the swing to trackers without changing inventory or health.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: super.swingItem starts the local swingTimer and arm render so the player sees instant feedback before any round trip. The new C0APacketAnimation line carries no fields, the server attributes it to the sending NetHandlerPlayServer connection. addToSendQueue flushes it to the server where it fans out as S0B animation to nearby trackers. Deleting this line keeps local visuals but hides swings from others, a common silent-aim artifact, while spamming it has no damage effect without a paired C02.

methods_detailed.name: dropOneItem
methods_detailed.detail_long: dropOneItem maps the boolean dropAll from the Q key handler to a C07PacketPlayerDigging Action enum, choosing DROP_ALL_ITEMS when true and DROP_ITEM for a single item. It constructs the packet with BlockPos.ORIGIN and EnumFacing.DOWN as dummy position and facing values because drops carry no block target. It queues the packet on sendQueue and returns null without spawning any EntityItem client-side, keeping inventory authoritative. The server NetHandlerPlayServer interprets the action, splits or clears the held stack, and spawns the EntityItem itself with pickup delay. Holding Ctrl-Q drives the dropAll path to empty the stack, while tapping Q drops one. Forging this C07 with modified actions is how drop-spam or inventory-desync exploits attempt to duplicate items, but the server re-validates the held stack. No S packet is produced locally here.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The ternary line translates the dropAll boolean into the exact C07 Action enum the server switches on, so the packet meaning hinges on that one enum value. The constructor uses BlockPos.ORIGIN and EnumFacing.DOWN as placeholders because the server ignores position for drop actions, unlike dig actions that need a real block. addToSendQueue sends the request without creating an EntityItem, proving drops are server-authoritative. Returning null signals no local entity to the caller, so blocking the packet means nothing drops and replaying it duplicates drop attempts the server must deduplicate.

methods_detailed.name: closeScreen
methods_detailed.detail_long: closeScreen reads openContainer.windowId as the server-assigned container ID so the close refers to the exact chest, furnace or custom GUI. It constructs C0DPacketCloseWindow with that ID and queues it on sendQueue to tell the server the client dismissed the screen. It then calls closeScreenAndDropStack which clears the cursor ItemStack via inventory.setItemStack null, calls super.closeScreen and calls mc.displayGuiScreen null to remove the GUI. The server NetHandlerPlayServer closes its Container on C0D, cancels pending slot transactions and may drop or retain the cursor stack. Sending a wrong windowId desyncs containers and can leave ghost items until the next S2E or S30 resync. This is a pure teardown with no item movement packet, so dupes that race C0E clicks against C0D rely on server ordering here.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The C0DPacketCloseWindow constructor captures openContainer.windowId at call time, binding the close to the currently open container instance. addToSendQueue delivers that ID to the server where NetHandlerPlayServer matches it against its own openContainer. closeScreenAndDropStack then nulls the dragged cursor stack and clears the GuiScreen locally, so visuals close even if the packet is delayed. If the C0D is dropped the server keeps the container open and later forces S2E close, which is why inventory-desync fixes always resync windowId.

methods_detailed.name: sendPlayerAbilities
methods_detailed.detail_long: sendPlayerAbilities wraps the live this.capabilities object, including isFlying, allowFlying, isCreativeMode, flySpeed and walkSpeed, into a new C13PacketPlayerAbilities. It queues that snapshot on sendQueue with no extra validation, trusting the caller in onLivingUpdate to have flipped the flags correctly for spectator, double-space or landing. It is called when spectator forces flight on, when double-space toggles flight, and when landing clears flight in non-spectator. The server compares the received flags against the authoritative GameType and op state, ignoring or kicking on illegal fly enable. Because the whole capabilities struct is sent, stale walkSpeed or flySpeed values can also leak to the server if mods mutate them. The receiver applies allowed changes and echoes the authoritative state back via S39, so a forged C13 only persists until the next S39 correction.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The one-line body constructs C13PacketPlayerAbilities from this.capabilities by reference copy, so every flag and speed at call time goes on the wire. addToSendQueue pushes it through NetHandlerPlayClient to NetHandlerPlayServer, which re-checks allowFlying against gamemode. The adjacent sendHorseJump and sendHorseInventory lines show the C0B RIDING_JUMP with power times 100 and OPEN_INVENTORY pattern, distinguishing ability sync from action packets. Tampering with capabilities before this call is the client fly-speed hack, corrected when the server replies with S39.

methods_detailed.name: respawnPlayer
methods_detailed.detail_long: respawnPlayer is bound to the death-screen respawn button and takes no position or health arguments because the server owns the spawn point. It constructs C16PacketClientStatus with EnumState.PERFORM_RESPAWN, the dedicated respawn enum distinct from OPEN_INVENTORY statistics states. It queues that packet on sendQueue so NetHandlerPlayServer can trigger ServerConfigurationManager respawn, clearing death, resetting health and food, and teleporting to spawn or bed. The client does not move itself or heal locally here, waiting for S07 respawn, S06 health and S21 chunk packets to rebuild state. Pressing the button twice queues duplicate C16s that the server idempotently ignores if already alive. Blocking this packet leaves the player on the death screen indefinitely, while forging it while alive is ignored by the server state check.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The constructor argument PERFORM_RESPAWN selects the respawn branch in NetHandlerPlayServer handleClientStatus, not a generic status update. addToSendQueue sends it over the established play channel, so it only works while connected to a server after death. The following damageEntity snippet shows local health subtraction is separate and not invoked here, proving respawn does not heal client-side. The server responds with position, health and inventory resyncs, so dropping C16 strands the client on the death GUI.

methods_detailed.name: onUpdate
methods_detailed.detail_long: onUpdate is the server per-tick driver that first calls theItemInWorldManager.updateBlockRemoving to progress survival mining cracks and creative breaks. It decrements respawnInvulnerabilityTicks and hurtResistantTime, then calls openContainer.detectAndSendChanges to push S2F, S30 and S31 slot deltas for the open GUI. If the open container no longer passes canInteractWith it forces closeScreen plus inventoryContainer reset to prevent out-of-range crafting. It then drains destroyedItemsNetCache in Integer.MAX_VALUE batches into S13PacketDestroyEntities so batched entity removals leave in one packet rather than spamming. It streams up to 10 queued loadedChunks per tick, checking isBlockLoaded and isPopulated, collecting tile entities for description packets and notifying the tracker. Single chunks go as S21PacketChunkData with mask 65535 while multiples go as S26PacketMapChunkBulk for bandwidth efficiency. Spectator follow at the end repositions the player to the spectated entity and calls serverUpdateMountedMovingPlayer.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The while loop drains destroyedItemsNetCache with an iterator remove, packing IDs into an int array sized to the queue length for one S13. sendPacket through playerNetServerHandler delivers the destroy batch only to this player, not a broadcast, and non-player removes are batched while player removes send immediately via removeEntity. The loadedChunks guard then builds a max-10 list per tick, throttling chunk bandwidth to avoid flooding the client on login or teleport. This batching is why mass mob clears arrive as few S13s and why chunk streaming staggers as S21 or S26 over multiple ticks.

methods_detailed.name: onUpdateEntity
methods_detailed.detail_long: onUpdateEntity runs after onUpdate and wraps everything in a crash-report context labeled Ticking player for debuggability. It first calls super.onUpdate for base entity aging and then scans the entire inventory for ItemStacks whose item isMap, calling createMapDataPacket for each held map and sending any non-null result directly. It compares live getHealth, foodStats.getFoodLevel and saturation-zero versus cached lastHealth, lastFoodLevel and wasHungry, sending S06PacketUpdateHealth only on a real delta to throttle health traffic. On send it copies current health, food and hungry flag into the caches so the next tick can detect the next change. It separately tracks combinedHealth as health plus absorption for scoreboard health objectives without spamming S06. It compares experienceTotal to lastExperience and on change sends S1FPacketSetExperience with experience, experienceTotal and experienceLevel progress. Every 20 times 5 ticks it checks exploreAllBiomes progress, which can later trigger achievements without extra packets here.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The inventory loop checks every slot for isMap and calls createMapDataPacket, which returns null when the map has no dirty columns, explaining intermittent map traffic. The health if compares three cached fields at once so saturation flipping to zero alone triggers S06 even if health and food are static. The S06 constructor carries health, food level and saturation that the client applies in setPlayerSPHealth, so suppressing it desyncs hearts. Updating lastHealth, lastFoodLevel and wasHungry right after send implements the throttle, and the following combinedHealth check drives scoreboards without extra network cost.

methods_detailed.name: displayGUIChest
methods_detailed.detail_long: displayGUIChest first closes any mismatched openContainer to avoid stacking windows, then checks for ILockableContainer with isLocked, canOpen lock code and isSpectator bypass. On denial it sends S02PacketChat with container.isLocked as type 2 above-hotbar message and S29PacketSoundEffect random.door_close at the player position, then returns without opening. On success it calls getNextWindowId which cycles currentWindowId modulo 100 plus 1 for the next S2D ID. If the inventory is an IInteractionObject it sends S2DPacketOpenWindow with that ID, the GUI ID string, display name and size, else it falls back to minecraft:container with a new ContainerChest. It then assigns openContainer.windowId to the new ID and calls onCraftGuiOpened to register this as ICrafting for S2F and S30 updates. The client uses the windowId to route all future C0E clicks, so a stale ID breaks container interaction until S2E close resyncs.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The isLocked plus canOpen plus isSpectator condition gates locked chests, letting spectators bypass the lock without a key. The S02 line builds a type-2 chat that renders above the hotbar instead of in chat history, carrying the locked-container translation. The S29 line plays door_close only to this player at their coordinates with volume 1 and pitch 1. The S2D lines bind currentWindowId to the GUI type and size, so the client opens the matching GuiChest or furnace screen and routes C0E clicks by that ID.

methods_detailed.name: displayVillagerTradeGui
methods_detailed.detail_long: displayVillagerTradeGui allocates a fresh window via getNextWindowId, then creates a ContainerMerchant from player inventory, villager and world and stamps it with currentWindowId. It registers the player via onCraftGuiOpened so slot changes stream as S2F and S30. It resolves the merchant inventory and display name, then sends S2DPacketOpenWindow with minecraft:villager, name and size to open the client GuiMerchant shell. It fetches MerchantRecipeList via villager.getRecipes, and if non-null allocates a PacketBuffer, writes the windowId int first, then serializes the recipe list with writeToBuf. It wraps that buffer in S3FPacketCustomPayload on channel MC|TrList so the client can populate trade arrows and prices. Without the S3F the GUI opens empty, and a mismatched windowId in the payload orphans recipes from the window. Closing later goes through S2E and container teardown.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: getNextWindowId cycles the window counter so each trade gets a unique ID for routing C0E clicks. The ContainerMerchant assignment plus onCraftGuiOpened wires server inventory sync before any packet, ensuring slot deltas have a listener. The S2D line opens the villager GUI shell with the merchant name and slot count the client uses to size the screen. The PacketBuffer sequence writes windowId then recipes into MC|TrList, which the client NetHandlerPlayClient matches back to the open window, so dropping S3F leaves a recipe-less merchant.

methods_detailed.name: closeScreen
methods_detailed.detail_long: closeScreen implements the server-initiated close path when canInteractWith fails, distance is exceeded, or a plugin forces dismissal. It sends S2EPacketCloseWindow carrying openContainer.windowId so the client tears down exactly the GUI it thinks is open. It then calls closeContainer which invokes onContainerClosed and resets openContainer to inventoryContainer, clearing crafting listeners. Unlike the client C0D path, this originates from the server and the client must obey by clearing its GuiScreen and cursor handling. If the windowId is stale the client may ignore the close until the next S2D or manual Esc, leaving a ghost container. No item stacks are moved here, pending C0E transactions for that window are invalidated. The paired client method sends C0D upward, while this sends S2E downward.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The S2E constructor captures the live openContainer.windowId, binding the close to the server idea of the open GUI. sendPacket pushes it only to this player, and closeContainer immediately resets to inventoryContainer so further C0E clicks for the old ID are rejected. The following updateHeldItem snippet shows cursor sync via S2F with -1 -1, which is separate and not sent on close. If S2E is lost the client keeps rendering the container while the server has already discarded it, causing click desync.

methods_detailed.name: sendPlayerAbilities
methods_detailed.detail_long: sendPlayerAbilities first null-guards playerNetServerHandler so early login or disconnect ticks do not throw when no channel exists. It sends S39PacketPlayerAbilities constructed from the authoritative this.capabilities, including allowFlying, isFlying, creative and speed fields owned by the server GameType. It then calls updatePotionMetadata to reconcile invisibility, color and ambience flags, which also re-notifies the tracker for spectators. It is invoked from setGameType, spectator mount changes and login capability sync. The client applies S39 directly to EntityPlayerSP capabilities, overriding any forged C13 until the next legitimate toggle. Because S39 carries the full struct, it also corrects flySpeed hacks in one round trip. Failure to send here after a gamemode switch leaves creative flight visually enabled but server-rejected.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The null check protects ticks where the NetHandler has not been assigned yet, such as construction or logout teardown. The S39 line serializes the server capabilities object, which the client must accept as authoritative over its local copy. updatePotionMetadata follows to keep DataWatcher flags and tracker visibility consistent, especially forcing spectators invisible. Blocking S39 after a gamemode change is how stale fly states persist client-side until movement validation kicks.

methods_detailed.name: setGameType
methods_detailed.detail_long: setGameType applies the new WorldSettings.GameType to theItemInWorldManager first so mining, interaction and damage rules change atomically. It sends S2BPacketChangeGameState with reason 3 and the game-type ID as float, which drives the client title, HUD and PlayerControllerMP rules. If the target is SPECTATOR it calls mountEntity null to dismount any vehicle before hiding, else it calls setSpectatingEntity self to exit camera mode. It then calls sendPlayerAbilities to push S39 flight and creative flags matching the new mode, plus markPotionsDirty to refresh effect visibility. The client PlayerControllerMP.setGameType mirrors the mode locally on S2B receipt. Skipping S39 here would leave survival flight enabled visually, while skipping the spectate reset would strand the camera. The sequence ensures abilities and camera never disagree with the authoritative mode.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The setGameType call on theItemInWorldManager flips server mining and block rules before any client notification, preventing a race where the client still mines as creative. The S2B line uses reason 3 which the client interprets as gamemode change, with the ID carried as float per protocol. The spectator branch dismounts or re-attaches the camera so S43 camera and S1B attach stay consistent. sendPlayerAbilities plus markPotionsDirty finish by pushing S39 and S1C metadata, so all three channels agree on the new mode.

methods_detailed.name: trySleep/wakeUpPlayer/mountEntity
methods_detailed.detail_long: trySleep delegates to super.trySleep for bed checks on distance, time and occupancy, and only on EnumStatus OK proceeds to networking. It builds S0APacketUseBed with this player and bed BlockPos, broadcasts it via getEntityTracker.sendToAllTrackingEntity so nearby clients render the lying pose, then calls setPlayerLocation to force-resync position and sends the same packet directly to the sleeper. wakeUpPlayer checks isPlayerSleeping, then broadcasts S0BPacketAnimation with ID 2 to trackers to stand the model up before calling super and re-syncing position if a handler exists. mountEntity captures the prior ridingEntity, calls super.mountEntity, and on change sends S1BPacketEntityAttach with type 0 binding this to the new ridingEntity plus a setPlayerLocation correction. Together they keep bed, wake and ride states visible to all trackers while the mover gets an authoritative teleport. Missing S1B or S0A leaves remote clients showing standing or dismounted ghosts.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: super.trySleep validates the bed and returns OK only when sleep is legal, gating all packets on that enum. The S0A constructor binds the player entity ID to the bed position so remote clients can orient the lying model. sendToAllTrackingEntity fans S0A to trackers while the direct sendPacket plus setPlayerLocation ensures the sleeper also snaps to the bed. wakeUpPlayer mirrors this with S0B animation 2 and mountEntity with S1B attach 0, so blocking any of them desyncs pose or vehicle attachment.

methods_detailed.name: onNewPotionEffect/onFinishedPotionEffect
methods_detailed.detail_long: onNewPotionEffect and onChangedPotionEffect both call their super implementations to update the server effect map, then send S1DPacketEntityEffect with getEntityId and the PotionEffect object carrying ID, amplifier, duration, ambient and particles. This covers both fresh application and amplifier or duration refreshes from beacons or splash potions. onFinishedPotionEffect calls super to remove the effect, then sends S1EPacketRemoveEntityEffect with entity ID and the finished effect so the client clears particles and attribute modifiers. The client applies S1D by adding or replacing the effect and S1E by removing it, keeping DataWatcher color in sync via later metadata. Without these pushes the client would show wrong hearts, speed or invisibility until the next S1C. The tracker burst in updatePlayerEntity also replays active effects via S1D on first sight, so late-joining trackers converge.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: super calls mutate the server PotionEffect map first so the packet reflects committed state rather than a prediction. The S1D constructor packs entity ID plus the full effect struct, letting the client reproduce duration and amplifier exactly. The S1E constructor packs entity ID plus effect ID for removal, clearing client overlays and modifiers. Dropping S1D leaves the client missing particles while the server applies damage or speed, and dropping S1E leaves ghost effects after expiry.

methods_detailed.name: updatePlayerList
methods_detailed.detail_long: updatePlayerList runs each server tick and first checks firstUpdateDone or distance squared over 16 to decide whether to rescan tracking membership via updatePlayerEntities. It detects ridingEntity changes or a 60-tick refresh and broadcasts S1BPacketEntityAttach type 0 so vehicle mounts stay glued on remote clients. For EntityItemFrame every 10 ticks it re-sends map data for displayed ItemMaps and forces sendMetadataToAllAssociatedPlayers for frame rotation. The main motion gate fires when updateCounter modulo updateFrequency is zero, isAirBorne is true, or DataWatcher reports a change, ensuring idle entities still heartbeat. Inside it encodes positions times 32 and rotations times 256 over 360, computes deltas against encoded caches, and sets flag for 4-unit move and flag1 for 4-unit look change. It chooses S15 rel-move, S16 look, S17 look-move or S18 teleport based on the 128-unit byte range, 400-tick forced teleport, ridingEntity and onGround flip, then handles S12 velocity and S19 head look. Finally it increments updateCounter and flushes velocityChanged via func_151261_b.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The outer modulo plus isAirBorne plus hasObjectChanged condition throttles per-type updates, for example mobs every 3 ticks versus arrows every 20, while forcing immediate send on motion or metadata dirt. The times-32 and times-256 encoding lines convert doubles to fixed-point protocol units the client decodes, matching S14 byte deltas and S18 int positions. The flag and flag1 thresholds of 4 encoded units filter sub-pixel jitter to save bandwidth. The inner range check on -128 to 128 plus 400-tick and onGround tests selects cheap S14 deltas versus authoritative S18 teleport, which is why large teleports or long drift always correct with S18.

methods_detailed.name: updatePlayerEntity
methods_detailed.detail_long: updatePlayerEntity manages one candidate player against one tracked entity, skipping when the player is the tracked entity itself to avoid self-tracking loops. It calls func_180233_c for XZ range plus spectator visibility, then requires either chunk watch via isPlayerWatchingThisChunk or forceSpawn to admit a new tracker. On admission it adds to trackingPlayers, sends createSpawnPacket as the entity-type-correct S0C, S0E, S0F, S10 or S11 birth packet, then follows with S1C metadata if the DataWatcher is non-blank. It sends S49 NBT when getNBTTagCompound is non-null, S20 attributes for watched collections, and caches motion into lastTracked fields for future S12 deltas. It sends S12 velocity immediately unless the spawn was S0F mob which already carries motion, then replays S1B attach for riding or leashed states, S04 equipment for five armor slots, S0A bed if sleeping, and S1D for each active potion. On range exit it removes from trackingPlayers and calls removeEntity which emits S13 destroy, keeping client worlds garbage-collected.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The self-inequality plus func_180233_c plus isPlayerWatchingThisChunk chain ensures a player only receives entities in range, in a watched chunk and visible through spectator rules. createSpawnPacket returns the polymorphic birth packet the client needs to allocate the entity shell with correct ID and position. The S1C and S49 follow-ups hydrate DataWatcher flags and tile NBT that the spawn packet alone cannot carry. Missing this burst leaves invisible or untextured entities, while the else-branch S13 destroy on range exit is what removes them when walking away.

methods_detailed.name: createSpawnPacket
methods_detailed.detail_long: createSpawnPacket is a type-switch factory that warns when the entity isDead yet still requested, then returns the exact spawn packet for each class. EntityItem maps to S0E type 2 data 1, EntityPlayerMP to S0C spawn player, minecarts to S0E type 10 with network ID, boats to S0E type 1, and IAnimals plus other EntityLivingBase to S0F mob with head yaw refresh. Projectiles use fixed S0E type IDs including 60 arrow with shooter ID, 61 snowball, 62 egg, 65 pearl, 72 eye, 73 potion with damage, 75 bottle, 76 firework, 90 fish hook with angler fallback, plus fireballs 63, 64 small, 66 wither with acceleration scaled by 8000. FallingBlock uses S0E 70 with Block.getStateId, armor stands 78, XP orbs S11, paintings S10 and item frames or leash knots S0E 71 or 77 with overridden fixed-point hanging coordinates. Any unknown class throws IllegalArgumentException, failing fast rather than sending a corrupt spawn. The caller updatePlayerEntity sends the result before metadata, attributes and equipment so the client has an ID to attach them to.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: Each branch constructs S0E with the hardcoded vanilla type ID the client uses to pick a renderer and physics, so 60 versus 61 versus 73 is not interchangeable. The arrow line threads shootingEntity ID with a self-ID fallback when the shooter is gone, letting the client attribute kill credit. The potion line passes getPotionDamage as the data int so the client shows the correct splash color and effect. Sending the wrong ID or data spawns the wrong visual or crashes old clients, which is why the final else throws instead of guessing.

methods_detailed.name: sendMetadataToAllAssociatedPlayers
methods_detailed.detail_long: sendMetadataToAllAssociatedPlayers first fetches the trackedEntity DataWatcher and checks hasObjectChanged to avoid spamming identical S1C packets every tick. On dirty it calls func_151261_b with S1CPacketEntityMetadata carrying entity ID, watcher and false for non-initial, which fans out to trackers plus the tracked player if it is an EntityPlayerMP. It then checks for EntityLivingBase, pulls the ServersideAttributeMap, and reads getAttributeInstanceSet as the delta set of recently modified max-health, speed or attack attributes. If that set is non-empty it sends S20PacketEntityProperties with the set through func_151261_b and immediately clears the set to prevent resend on the next tick. This two-channel push keeps flags like sneaking, hurt color and custom names via S1C separate from numeric attributes via S20. The method is called after every movement send and every 10 ticks for item frames, so metadata converges quickly. Suppressing it leaves ghost names or stale health scaling.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The hasObjectChanged guard reads the DataWatcher dirty flag set by updateObject calls, so S1C is only built when a watched byte actually flipped. func_151261_b is used instead of sendPacketToTrackedPlayers so the tracked player itself also receives its own metadata for self-render like skin flags. The attribute set fetch plus isEmpty check isolates numeric modifier changes that DataWatcher cannot express, sending them as S20. The trailing clear resets the delta set, meaning a lost S20 will not auto-retry until the attribute changes again.

methods_detailed.name: sendPacketToTrackedPlayers/func_151261_b
methods_detailed.detail_long: sendPacketToTrackedPlayers iterates the trackingPlayers hash set and calls playerNetServerHandler.sendPacket for each member, delivering movement, look, metadata or velocity to exactly those in range. It performs no range recheck itself, relying on updatePlayerEntity and func_180233_c to maintain set membership, which makes it a cheap fan-out on the hot tick path. func_151261_b wraps it by first calling sendPacketToTrackedPlayers, then checking if trackedEntity is an EntityPlayerMP and echoing the same packet to that entity own channel. That self-include variant is used for S1C metadata, S20 attributes and S12 velocityChanged where the subject player must also see its own flags or knockback. Using the wrong helper hides self-effects like potion color or takes no knockback visually. Both take a generic Packet so S14, S18, S19 and S1B all flow through the same loop. The design separates observer sync from subject sync with one branch.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The for loop over trackingPlayers shows the fan-out cost scales with observer count, each sendPacket queuing on that player Netty channel. The packetIn parameter is opaque, so the same loop carries tiny S14 deltas and large S20 lists without branching. func_151261_b adds the instanceof EntityPlayerMP self-echo, which is required because a player does not track itself in trackingPlayers. Choosing between the two controls whether the subject sees its own S12 knockback or S1C name flags, a frequent source of self-desync bugs when misused.

methods_detailed.name: removeFromTrackedPlayers/removeTrackedPlayerSymmetric
methods_detailed.detail_long: sendDestroyEntityPacketToTrackedPlayers loops trackingPlayers and calls removeEntity on each, which for players sends immediate S13 and for other entities queues into destroyedItemsNetCache for batched S13. removeFromTrackedPlayers checks contains before acting, then calls playerMP.removeEntity to destroy the client-side copy and removes the player from the set to stop future sends. removeTrackedPlayerSymmetric is the symmetric alias used on chunk unload or dimension change, performing the same contains, remove and removeEntity sequence. Together they ensure no stale entity shells linger after range exit, logout or chunk unload. Forgetting the removeEntity call leaks ghost mobs that float until the next S18 or relog. The S13 carries only entity IDs, so the client looks up and deletes the matching world entry. These paths are the only clean teardown for tracker membership.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The destroy loop delegates to EntityPlayerMP.removeEntity, which decides between instant S13 for players and batched cache for others, explaining why player logouts vanish instantly. The contains guard prevents double-destroy S13s that would make the client delete a reused entity ID. removeEntity triggers the S13 with the tracked entity ID so the client can free the renderer and physics. The symmetric variant repeats this pattern for unload paths, so skipping either leaves ghost entities that still receive S14 moves.

methods_detailed.name: func_180233_c
methods_detailed.detail_long: func_180233_c computes d0 as player X minus encodedPosX divided by 32 and d1 as player Z minus encodedPosZ divided by 32, converting the fixed-point cache back to block units. It checks d0 and d1 against plus and minus trackingDistanceThreshold, which varies by entity type such as 64 for items or 512 for dragons. It also calls trackedEntity.isSpectatedByPlayer to enforce spectator invisibility, hiding non-spectated entities from spectator cameras and vice versa. It ignores Y distance entirely, so vertical range does not gate tracking in 1.8.9. The result gates updatePlayerEntity admission and retention, preventing bandwidth waste on far entities. A false return triggers removal plus S13 destroy, while true plus chunk watch triggers the full spawn burst. Cheats cannot force the server to send out-of-range entities because this gate runs before every send.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The d0 and d1 lines decode the last-sent position by integer-dividing the fixed-point cache, noting the int division truncation before cast. The long return line ANDs four range comparisons with isSpectatedByPlayer, so all five must pass to keep tracking. isPlayerWatchingThisChunk below adds a second chunk-visibility requirement checked alongside this gate in updatePlayerEntity. Together they explain why entities pop in at chunk borders or vanish when spectating, and why radar hacks cannot see beyond trackingDistanceThreshold.

methods_detailed.name: initializeConnectionToPlayer
methods_detailed.detail_long: initializeConnectionToPlayer builds the login burst for a new EntityPlayerMP after NBT load. It resolves the profile name, caches the profile, reads player NBT, binds world and ItemInWorldManager, and logs IP with entityId and coordinates. It sets game type, creates NetHandlerPlayServer and sends S01 JoinGame with entityId, game type, hardcore, dimension, difficulty, max players, terrain and reduced debug. It then sends MC|Brand S3F, S41 difficulty, S05 spawn, S39 abilities and S09 held change. It pushes stats, achievements and full scoreboard, broadcasts the join message and registers the player in the roster. It teleports with setPlayerLocation S08, syncs time and weather, applies resource pack and re-sends potion effects with S1D. Riding NBT is restored by spawning the mount entity.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The NetHandlerPlayServer construction binds the channel to the player entity. S01PacketJoinGame carries entityId, game type, dimension and difficulty so the client can build WorldClient. The MC|Brand S3F advertises server mod name for client display. S41, S05, S39 and S09 sync difficulty lock, spawn point, fly flags and held slot. sendScoreboard plus stats complete the burst before S08 position arrives.

methods_detailed.name: allowUserToConnect
methods_detailed.detail_long: allowUserToConnect enforces login gates in fixed order and returns a kick reason or null. First it checks profile bans via bannedPlayers, appending ban reason and formatted expiry date if present. Second it checks whitelist via canJoin, returning not white-listed when enforced and the player is neither op nor listed. Third it checks IP bans via bannedIPs with reason and expiry formatting. Fourth it checks capacity where list size at or above maxPlayers and no bypass returns server is full. Null means all gates passed and NetHandlerLoginServer may proceed to compression and LoginSuccess. The order matters because bans outrank whitelist and capacity. No packets are sent here, the caller closes with S00 using the returned string.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The bannedPlayers entry lookup builds the profile-ban string with reason and optional expiry date. The canJoin else-if enforces whitelist after profile bans so banned players cannot bypass via listing. The bannedIPs branch mirrors the profile logic for address bans with expiry formatting. The final else encodes capacity as size at or above maxPlayers without bypass returning server is full else null. Returning null is the only success path to S02 LoginSuccess.

methods_detailed.name: recreatePlayerEntity
methods_detailed.detail_long: recreatePlayerEntity respawns a dead player while reusing the NetHandlerPlayServer connection. It untracks the old entity from tracker and player manager, removes it dangerously and drops it from the roster. It copies dimension, creates a fresh ItemInWorldManager and EntityPlayerMP, then reuses the handler, clones inventory and stats, and preserves entityId and command stats. It resolves bed spawn via getBedSpawnLocation and places at plus 0.5 plus 0.1 offsets, or sends S2B state zero when the bed is invalid. It loads the chunk, lifts the player above collision up to Y 256, sends S07 Respawn, S08 location via setPlayerLocation, S05 spawn and S1F experience. It resyncs time and weather, re-adds to manager and world, restores maps and heals. No kick occurs.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The bed null check skips spawn logic for world-spawn respawns. getBedSpawnLocation validates the bed, with plus 0.5 and plus 0.1 offsets centering the player on respawn. Invalid beds send S2B state zero to show the respawn-screen message. The chunk load plus while-collision lift to Y 256 prevents suffocation on respawn. S07 Respawn plus setPlayerLocation S08 rebuild the client world and pin the position.

methods_detailed.name: transferPlayerToDimension
methods_detailed.detail_long: transferPlayerToDimension moves a live player across dimensions without dropping the connection. It records the old dimension, sets the new id and sends S07 Respawn with difficulty, terrain and game type so the client rebuilds WorldClient. It removes the player dangerously, clears isDead, scales coordinates through transferEntityToWorld with factor 8.0 between overworld and nether clamped to border, or spawn point for end. It re-registers with preparePlayer, pins position with setPlayerLocation S08, rebinds ItemInWorldManager world and resyncs time and weather. It then syncs inventory and re-sends every active S1D potion effect. No kick occurs, failure leaves the player in the new world at the portal exit.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: Saving old dimension i preserves the source for coordinate scaling. S07PacketRespawn forces the client to swap WorldClient before the entity moves. removePlayerEntityDangerously plus isDead false detach from the old world without death drops. transferEntityToWorld applies times or divide by 8.0 clamping plus portal placement. setPlayerLocation S08, inventory sync and S1D effect loop complete the handoff so buffs survive travel.

methods_detailed.name: playerLoggedIn
methods_detailed.detail_long: playerLoggedIn joins the roster and announces presence with S38 tab-list packets. It appends to playerEntityList and uuidToPlayerMap for lookups and duplicate detection. It broadcasts S38 ADD_PLAYER for the newcomer to all existing players via sendPacketToAllPlayers. It spawns the entity in the dimension world and registers with preparePlayer to load chunks and tracking. It then loops the full roster and sends each existing ADD_PLAYER to the newcomer so tab lists converge symmetrically. No kick or teleport occurs here, position was already set by initializeConnectionToPlayer. Duplicate logins are handled earlier by createPlayerForUser kicking the old session.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: Adding to list and uuid map makes the player visible to commands and duplicate checks. The broadcast S38 ADD_PLAYER informs all clients to create tab-list entries. spawnEntityInWorld plus preparePlayer load the chunk and start entity tracking. The loop sends the full existing roster as individual S38 ADD_PLAYER packets to the newcomer. This two-way exchange keeps tab lists consistent on join.

methods_detailed.name: playerLoggedOut
methods_detailed.detail_long: playerLoggedOut persists and removes a disconnecting player. It triggers leaveGameStat, writes NBT and stats via writePlayerData, and removes any ridden mount dangerously. It removes the player entity and its tracker entry, drops it from playerEntityList, and clears uuidToPlayerMap and stat files only if the mapped entry is identical. It broadcasts S38 REMOVE_PLAYER to remaining players so tab lists drop the entry. No packets go to the leaver because the channel is closing. The method is called from NetHandlerPlayServer onDisconnect after the quit message. Failure to remove from maps would leave ghost tab entries and block relogin.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: triggerAchievement plus writePlayerData flush stats and NBT before removal. The ridingEntity check removes horse, boat or pig mounts to avoid orphan vehicles. removeEntity plus removePlayer plus list removal detach tracking and roster membership. The identity check before map removal protects against deleting a newer duplicate login. The final S38 REMOVE_PLAYER broadcast tells clients to purge the tab entry.

methods_detailed.name: updateTimeAndWeatherForPlayer
methods_detailed.detail_long: updateTimeAndWeatherForPlayer syncs border, clock and rain to one player after login, respawn or dimension change. It sends S44 WorldBorder INITIALIZE from the overworld border so the client enforces the same center and size. It sends S03 TimeUpdate with total time, day time and doDaylightCycle gamerule. If the target world isRaining it sends S2B state 1 to start rain, state 7 with rain strength and state 8 with thunder strength. Clear weather sends only border and time with no S2B. No kick or teleport occurs. Clients apply rain strength gradually to render particles and sky darkening.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: Fetching the overworld border ensures nether and end players share the same boundary. S44 INITIALIZE carries center, size and warning timers in one packet. S03PacketTimeUpdate carries total age, day time and daylight-cycle flag to drive the sun. The isRaining gate adds S2B 1, 7 and 8 for rain begin plus strength lerps. Without rain the client keeps clear skies from the earlier world load.

methods_detailed.name: update
methods_detailed.detail_long: update runs every server tick for each EntityPlayerMP to maintain connection health and throttle counters. It first clears field_147366_g and increments networkTickCount, then opens a keepAlive profiler section. If more than 40 ticks elapsed since lastSentPingPacket it refreshes lastSentPingPacket and lastPingTime from nanoTime millis, stores the int key in field_147378_h and sends S00PacketKeepAlive with that key. It then decays chatSpamThresholdCount by one if positive and does the same for itemDropThreshold, which implements the 20 per message and 20 per creative drop leak. Finally it checks idle kick using getLastActiveTime and getMaxPlayerIdleMinutes, kicking with You have been idle for too long if exceeded. No teleport-back occurs here, only S00 send and conditional S40 kick. The method explains the 40 tick ping cadence and the spam decay loop.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The tick counter and keepAlive section frame the periodic work. The greater-than-40L gate throttles S00PacketKeepAlive so ping is sampled about every two seconds. lastPingTime and field_147378_h store the key that processKeepAlive must later echo to compute ping. S00PacketKeepAlive carries that int key to the client for round-trip timing. The chatSpamThresholdCount decrement implements one unit of leak per tick against the plus-20 per chat addition. The following itemDropThreshold block applies the same leak to creative drops.

methods_detailed.name: processPlayer
methods_detailed.detail_long: processPlayer is the authoritative movement validator for C03, C04, C05 and C06 packets on the net thread. It first rejects non-finite doubles or floats via func_183006_b and kicks with Invalid move packet received. It then handles special branches for riding entities, sleeping players and conquered End before normal walking. For normal moves it enforces absolute border abs greater than 3.0E7 with kick Illegal position. It enforces speed by comparing squared delta minus motion squared against 100.0D and teleporting back with setPlayerLocation S08 on violation. It enforces collision with a 0.0625F contracted box, flags moved-wrongly when residual delta exceeds 0.0625D, and teleport-backs if cheating through blocks. It enforces floating by counting ticks with fall less than minus 0.03125D threshold and kicking after 80 ticks when flight is not allowed. Riding divergence over 4.0D sends S18PacketEntityTeleport plus S08 correction.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The isMoving branch copies the claimed X Y Z into d8 d9 d10 for later reconciliation. The 3.0E7D absolute check kicks with Illegal position to enforce world border limits. The isRotating branch copies yaw and pitch into f1 f2 without yet applying position. onUpdateEntity and setPositionAndRotation rewind the player to last acked lastPos values so moveEntity can replay safely. The hasMoved false early return holds the player frozen until setPlayerLocation completes, which is the teleport-back mechanism. Cheat angles include ground-spoof via onGround flag and speed disablers that try to stay under the 100.0D delta gate.

methods_detailed.name: processChatMessage
methods_detailed.detail_long: processChatMessage handles inbound C01 chat and slash commands after PacketThreadUtil enqueue. If chat visibility is HIDDEN it replies with S02PacketChat chat.cannotSend in red and stops. Otherwise it marks the player active, normalizes whitespace with StringUtils.normalizeSpace and scans every char with ChatAllowedCharacters, kicking with Illegal characters in chat on failure. Strings starting with slash are delegated to handleSlashCommand and the command manager, others are broadcast as chat.type.text via sendChatMsgImpl. After dispatch it adds 20 to chatSpamThresholdCount and kicks with disconnect.spam if over 200 and the sender lacks command permission via canSendCommands. Ops and command-allowed players bypass the spam kick but still accumulate the counter. No teleport occurs, outcomes are S02 error reply, broadcast S02, or S40 kick.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: markPlayerActive resets idle time so chat counts as activity. normalizeSpace and the per-character isAllowedCharacter loop enforce the chat charset gate with kick on illegal characters. The startsWith slash branch separates commands from public broadcast via sendChatMsgImpl which fans out S02PacketChat. The plus-20 increment with greater-than-200 check implements the token bucket that update leaks by one per tick. The canSendCommands exemption lets ops burst without disconnect.spam kick, which spammers abuse by flooding just under the rate.

methods_detailed.name: processPlayerDigging
methods_detailed.detail_long: processPlayerDigging validates C07 dig, cancel, finish, drop and stop-use actions. DROP_ITEM and DROP_ALL_ITEMS are allowed only for non-spectators and call dropOneItem false or true. RELEASE_USE_ITEM calls stopUsingItem to end blocking or eating. For START, ABORT and STOP it computes squared distance from eye-adjusted player pos and silently returns if over 36.0D, which is six blocks reach. It also silently returns if block Y is at or above getBuildLimit. START checks isBlockProtected and world border contains, calling onBlockClicked on success or resyncing with S23PacketBlockChange on failure. STOP calls blockRemoving, ABORT calls cancelDestroyingBlock, then resends S23 if the block is still non-air. Invalid status throws IllegalArgumentException with no packet.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The d0 d1 d2 math builds eye-centered squared distance with plus 0.5 centering and plus 1.5 height offset. The greater-than-36.0D return silently drops over-reach digs without kick or resync. The buildLimit return blocks digs above world height. The START_DESTROY_BLOCK branch checks spawn protection and world border before allowing onBlockClicked. The else sends S23PacketBlockChange carrying server block state to force client resync on protected or out-of-border digs.

methods_detailed.name: processPlayerBlockPlacement
methods_detailed.detail_long: processPlayerBlockPlacement handles C08 right-click use-item and block activate. Direction 255 means use held item in air, calling tryUseItem if stack is non-null and returning early. Otherwise it checks build height with getBuildLimit minus one for upward faces and sends red S02PacketChat build.tooHigh when exceeded. For valid heights it requires hasMoved true, squared distance under 64.0D or eight blocks, no spawn protection and world border contains before calling activateBlockOrUseItem. Whether activated or denied it sets flag true to trigger dual S23PacketBlockChange resyncs for target and offset pos. Afterwards it clears zero-size stacks, copies the inventory slot when max use duration is zero, and corrects mismatched held stacks with S2FPacketSetSlot. Spectator and null-stack edges return without action.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The 255 direction branch isolates air-use like eating or throwing from block clicks. The buildLimit minus one check separates allowed placement from tooHigh, with UP faces held one lower. The hasMoved plus less-than-64.0D plus protection plus border line gates reach, teleport state, spawn guard and border in one condition. activateBlockOrUseItem carries offsets and facing to apply the actual placement or interaction. The else sends S02PacketChat build.tooHigh in red and the flag triggers S23 resyncs, which prevents ghost blocks.

methods_detailed.name: processClickWindow
methods_detailed.detail_long: processClickWindow validates C0E container clicks against the openContainer windowId and getCanCraft flag. Mismatched windowId or locked crafting is ignored entirely with no packet. Spectators bypass slotClick and get a full inventory resync via updateCraftingInventory. For survival players it calls slotClick and compares the result with the client predicted clickedItem via areItemStacksEqual. On match it sends S32PacketConfirmTransaction accepted true, then detectAndSendChanges and updateHeldItem. On mismatch it stores the action number in field_147372_n, sends S32 accepted false, locks further crafting with setCanCraft false and pushes the full server inventory list. The lock persists until C0F confirm with matching uid unlocks it. This is the classic desync recovery and dup-prevention gate.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: slotClick applies the server-side inventory logic for the given slot button and mode. areItemStacksEqual compares client prediction to server result to detect desync or cheating. The true branch sends S32 accepted true carrying windowId and action number to confirm the transaction. The false branch stores the action number in field_147372_n, sends S32 accepted false, and locks crafting with setCanCraft false. The slot loop plus updateCraftingInventory pushes authoritative stacks, and C0F must later echo the stored uid to unlock.

methods_detailed.name: processUseEntity
methods_detailed.detail_long: processUseEntity validates C02 interact and attack after enqueue on the server thread. It resolves the entity from the world by ID and marks the player active, ignoring null entities silently. It computes visibility via canEntityBeSeen to select reach squared 36.0D when visible or 9.0D when not, which is six versus three blocks. If squared distance exceeds the gate the packet is dropped with no response. INTERACT calls interactWith, INTERACT_AT forwards hitVec to interactAt for armor stands and villagers. ATTACK kicks with Attempting to attack an invalid entity plus server warning if target is EntityItem, EntityXPOrb, EntityArrow or self. Otherwise it calls attackTargetEntityWithCurrentItem to apply damage and enchants. No S packets are sent here except the kick disconnect.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: canEntityBeSeen selects the reach gate of 36.0 versus 9.0 squared to stop wall-hit kill aura. The getDistanceSqToEntity less-than-d0 check drops out-of-reach uses without kick to tolerate lag. INTERACT versus INTERACT_AT separates leash and trade from precise hit-vector armor-stand poses. The ATTACK instanceof chain identifies invalid targets like items, XP orbs, arrows and self that normal clients never hit. The kick plus logWarning punishes packet-forged attacks, a common kill-aura and crash exploit probe.

methods_detailed.name: processKeepAlive
methods_detailed.detail_long: processKeepAlive handles C00 echo replies used for ping measurement. It runs on netty without PacketThreadUtil enqueue because it only touches volatile timing fields. It compares the echoed key to field_147378_h set by update when S00 was sent. Only exact match updates ping, stale or forged keys are ignored with no kick. On match it computes delta as currentTimeMillis nano millis minus lastPingTime. It smooths ping with weighted average ping times three plus delta divided by four. No packets are sent in response and no kick or teleport occurs. This explains why disabler cheats delay or spoof keepalive to fake lag without triggering fails.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The getKey equals field_147378_h gate ensures only the latest S00 echo counts. currentTimeMillis minus lastPingTime yields round-trip millis using nanoTime resolution. The ping times three plus i divided by four formula smooths jitter across samples. Ignoring mismatched keys avoids penalizing reordered packets, which is why timing disablers hold keepalives to simulate lag.

methods_detailed.name: handleJoinGame
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleJoinGame processes S01 on the client thread via PacketThreadUtil and builds the initial WorldClient. It installs a new PlayerControllerMP, then constructs WorldClient from gameType, hardcore flag, world type, dimension, difficulty and profiler. It copies difficulty into gameSettings, loads the world, sets thePlayer dimension and shows GuiDownloadTerrain. It assigns the server entityId, stores maxPlayers in currentServerMaxPlayers and applies reducedDebug. It sets the controller gameType, pushes client settings to the server and sends C17 MC|Brand with ClientBrandRetriever mod name. No kick occurs here, the reply packets are C17 brand and settings. Failure to receive later S08 keeps the download screen up.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: checkThreadAndEnqueue hops S01 onto the main client thread before touching the world. The WorldClient constructor carries gameType, hardcore, world type, dimension and difficulty that define physics and rendering. loadWorld plus GuiDownloadTerrain blocks input until terrain and S08 arrive. setEntityId and currentServerMaxPlayers bind the local player to the server id and tab-list cap. The final C17 MC|Brand reply advertises vanilla or modded client to the server.

methods_detailed.name: handlePlayerPosLook
methods_detailed.detail_long: handlePlayerPosLook applies S08 server teleports and corrections on the client thread. It reads absolute X Y Z yaw pitch, then adds current player pos or rotation when relative flags X Y Z Y_ROT X_ROT are present. For absolute axes it zeroes motionX, motionY or motionZ to stop rubber-band sliding. It then calls setPositionAndRotation and immediately replies with C06 PacketPlayerPosLook using posX, bounding-box minY, posZ, yaw, pitch and false onGround. On first receipt when doneLoadingTerrain is false it snapshots prevPos, sets the flag true and closes the download screen. Later receipts just correct position without GUI change. No kick occurs, the only response is the C03 C06 ack which lets the server clear hasMoved.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The X_ROT and Y_ROT flag checks add current pitch and yaw for relative look teleports. setPositionAndRotation applies the final merged coordinates and angles to the local player. The C06 reply carries bounding-box minY and false onGround so the server can validate the ack. The doneLoadingTerrain false branch fires once to initialize prevPos and dismiss GuiDownloadTerrain. Repeated S08 packets cause server-side teleport-backs that clients must ack to avoid movement freeze.

methods_detailed.name: handleSpawnObject
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleSpawnObject spawns S0E vehicles, projectiles and blocks in WorldClient. It scales network X Y Z by dividing by 32.0D to get block coordinates. It switches on type where 10 is minecart with subtype, 60 arrow, 61 snowball, 62 egg, 63 large fireball, 64 small fireball, 65 ender pearl, 66 wither skull, 71 item frame, 72 eye, 73 potion, 75 bottle, 76 firework, 77 leash, 78 armor stand, 1 boat, 2 item, 50 TNT, 51 crystal, 70 falling block and 90 fish hook. Fish hook resolves the thrower entity and resets data to zero, frames and leashes floor coords and reset data. After creation it copies serverPos, converts yaw and pitch with times 360 divided by 256, fixes multipart ids, sets entityId and adds to world. If data is positive it sets velocity divided by 8000.0D and links arrows to shooter living base.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: checkThreadAndEnqueue ensures spawning happens on the render thread. Dividing by 32.0D converts fixed-point network coords to doubles for accurate placement. The type 10 branch builds minecarts with network subtype for chest, furnace and TNT variants. The type 90 branch looks up the thrower player to attach the fish hook and clears extra data. Later code scales yaw and pitch by 360 over 256 and velocity by 8000, which cheats cannot spoof without server correction.

methods_detailed.name: handleChunkData
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleChunkData applies S21 chunk column load or unload on the client thread. If the packet is a full-chunk preChunk signal it checks extracted size, where zero means unload via doPreChunk false and return. Non-zero calls doPreChunk true to allocate the column. It then invalidates the 16 by 256 by 16 receive region, fetches the Chunk object and fills it with extracted bytes, size and full flag. It marks the block range for render update so lighting and meshes rebuild. If not a full chunk or the provider is not surface world, it resets relight checks to avoid stale skylight. Unloads free memory while loads populate blocks and biomes. No reply packet is sent.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The func_149274_i gate distinguishes full-column init from delta updates. Zero extracted size with full flag means unload, so doPreChunk false drops the column. Non-zero calls doPreChunk true then fillChunk with the compressed byte payload. invalidateBlockReceiveRegion and markBlockRangeForRenderUpdate bracket the fill to refresh lighting and rendering. The surface-world check skips relight reset for nether and end where skylight differs.

methods_detailed.name: handleConfirmTransaction
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleConfirmTransaction processes S32 server inventory verdicts on the client thread. It resolves the target container by windowId, where zero means inventoryContainer and otherwise the openContainer only if ids match. Null containers from stale windows are ignored. If the packet reports accepted false via func_148888_e it replies with C0F confirm accepted true carrying the same windowId and action number. Accepted true packets need no reply because both sides agree. The C0F reply unlocks the server-side canCraft lock set by processClickWindow mismatch. This single round trip resyncs duped or ghost clicks. No kick or teleport occurs.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: checkThreadAndEnqueue moves the verdict to the main thread. The windowId zero versus openContainer match selects inventory versus chest, furnace or crafting table. Null from closed windows is dropped to avoid acting on stale ids. The not-accepted check via func_148888_e triggers a C0F with accepted true to acknowledge the server correction. That C0F carries windowId and action number so the server can clear field_147372_n and re-enable crafting.

methods_detailed.name: handleRespawn
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleRespawn rebuilds WorldClient on S07 dimension change or difficulty sync. It first compares packet dimension to thePlayer dimension to detect cross-dimension moves. On change it clears doneLoadingTerrain, preserves the old scoreboard, constructs a new WorldClient with gameType, hardcore flag, world type, dimension and difficulty, then loads it and shows GuiDownloadTerrain. It always calls setDimensionAndSpawnPlayer and setGameType from the packet even for same-dimension respawns. The scoreboard carry-over keeps teams and objectives across deaths. No reply packet is sent, the client waits for follow-up S08 position and S21 chunks. This explains respawn flicker and why mods must rebind world references.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The dimension mismatch gate separates full world rebuild from same-world respawn. Clearing doneLoadingTerrain forces the next S08 to dismiss the download screen. Saving and restoring the scoreboard preserves teams across dimension travel. The WorldClient constructor with gameType and difficulty reapplies rules for the new dimension. The final setDimensionAndSpawnPlayer plus setGameType sync player controller even when no rebuild occurred.

methods_detailed.name: handleResourcePack
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleResourcePack implements S48 server pack prompt with C19 status replies. It extracts URL and hash, then branches on level slash slash prefix for local saves versus remote packs. Local files under saves are checked with isFile, replying ACCEPTED then async SUCCESSFULLY_LOADED or FAILED_DOWNLOAD, or immediate FAILED_DOWNLOAD if missing. Remote packs check ServerData resource mode where ENABLED auto-accepts and downloads, DISABLED replies DECLINED, and PROMPT schedules a GuiYesNo dialog. Confirming yes sets mode ENABLED, sends ACCEPTED and downloads, while no sets DISABLED and sends DECLINED. Downloads use the repository with Futures callbacks that send final C19 status. No kick occurs directly, but servers may kick on DECLINED.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: getURL and getHash provide the pack location and integrity hash for C19 replies. The startsWith level branch strips the prefix and resolves the file under the saves directory. isFile success sends C19 ACCEPTED immediately before async load. The Futures callbacks send SUCCESSFULLY_LOADED or FAILED_DOWNLOAD after the repository finishes. The missing-file else sends FAILED_DOWNLOAD, while remote ENABLED, DISABLED and PROMPT branches below handle server-hosted packs.

methods_detailed.name: handleCustomPayload
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleCustomPayload dispatches S3F plugin channels on the client thread. MC|TrList reads an int windowId, checks the current screen is GuiMerchant and ids match openContainer, then parses MerchantRecipeList and sets villager recipes. MC|Brand reads a string up to 32767 and stores it as clientBrand for server identification. MC|BOpen checks the held item is written_book and opens GuiScreenBook read-only. After TrList the buffer is released in finally to avoid leaks, other branches release via network layer. Unknown channels are ignored. No reply packet is sent, the data only mutates GUI and NBT state. Exploit angle is fake TrList with mismatched windowId which is correctly dropped.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The MC|TrList equals gate isolates villager trades from brand and book channels. readInt plus GuiMerchant plus windowId match prevents injecting trades into the wrong container. readFromBuf and setRecipes populate the merchant GUI with server offers. The catch logs load failures while finally releases the buffer to prevent netty leaks. The MC|Brand branch stores the server brand string for F3 debug display.
