methods_detailed.name: addWeatherEffect
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method is the server entry point for global weather entities such as lightning bolts. It first calls super.addWeatherEffect to register the entity in the world simulation and validate placement. Only if super returns true does any network fan-out occur, otherwise it returns false with no packets. On success it calls ServerConfigurationManager.sendToAllNear using the entity exact posX posY posZ coordinates. The radius is fixed at 512.0D and the call is gated by provider.getDimensionId so only players in the same dimension receive it. The packet constructed is S2CPacketSpawnGlobalEntity wrapping the entity instance. This large 512 block radius reflects that lightning is a sky-visible global event. Compared to 16.0D sound or 64.0D block-action ranges, this is intentionally wide. No batching is used because each strike is a discrete spawn.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The boolean method signature takes the weather Entity to spawn. The super call gates all networking on simulation acceptance. The sendToAllNear line builds S2CPacketSpawnGlobalEntity from the entity and passes 512.0D plus dimension ID for gating. The true branch returns success after queuing the broadcast. The else branch returns false with no packet when super rejects. This shows dimension-gated wide-radius spawn fan-out.

methods_detailed.name: newExplosion
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method runs the full server explosion simulation then notifies nearby clients. It first constructs an Explosion object with entity source, coordinates, strength, and flaming and smoking flags. It then calls doExplosionA for block resistance calculation and doExplosionB with false for no fire spawning here. If isSmoking is false it clears the affected block position list so clients receive an empty list. It then iterates directly over playerEntities belonging to this WorldServer dimension instance. Each player is distance checked with getDistanceSq against x y z with threshold 4096.0D which equals 64 blocks squared. Only players inside that sphere get a direct S27PacketExplosion via playerNetServerHandler.sendPacket. The packet carries x y z strength block list and per-player Vec3 knockback from getPlayerKnockbackMap. No explicit dimension check is needed because playerEntities are already dimension scoped.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature accepts source entity, position, strength, and flags. The next three lines create the Explosion and run both phases. The isSmoking check empties the block list for non-destructive blasts. The loop plus distanceSq less than 4096.0D gates recipients to a 64 block radius. The sendPacket line constructs S27PacketExplosion with strength, block list, and per-player knockback Vec3. This is direct per-player send, not chunk-scoped.

methods_detailed.name: sendQueuedBlockEvents
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method flushes the double-buffered block event queue at end of tick. The queue consists of two ServerBlockEventList buffers with blockEventCacheIndex selecting the active fill buffer. The while loop continues until the current read buffer is empty, handling events added during flushing. It snapshots the read index into i then flips blockEventCacheIndex with xor 1 so new addBlockEvent calls go to the other buffer. For each BlockEventData it calls fireBlockEvent to verify the block still matches and to run onBlockEventReceived. Only if validation returns true does it broadcast via sendToAllNear. That broadcast uses the event position coordinates with fixed 64.0D radius gated by provider.getDimensionId. The packet is S24PacketBlockAction built from position, block, event ID, and event parameter. Finally it clears the processed buffer list before looping.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The private method takes no args and loops on the active queue. The index snapshot plus xor flip implements double buffering. The for loop iterates BlockEventData entries in the frozen buffer. The fireBlockEvent condition gates packet construction on block match and handler acceptance. The sendToAllNear line shows 64.0D radius, dimension gating, and S24PacketBlockAction args. The clear call resets the buffer for the next tick.

methods_detailed.name: setEntityState
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method forwards a single-byte entity status to all tracking viewers. It does not implement its own radius check with 16.0D or 64.0D or 512.0D values. Instead it delegates viewer selection to EntityTracker via getEntityTracker. The tracker determines who currently tracks the entity based on tracking range and type. The packet created is S19PacketEntityStatus wrapping the entity and state byte. Typical states include hurt flash, totem use, tame hearts, and other entity events. The call func_151248_b performs the fan-out to that viewer set. Because WorldServer owns theEntityTracker field, this keeps visibility logic centralized. No dimension check appears here because tracker entries are already per-world.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment identifies this as Packet 38 entity status handling. The method signature takes entity and byte state. The body delegates to EntityTracker func_151248_b for viewer resolution. The constructor S19PacketEntityStatus binds entity ID and status byte into the packet. The trailing comment marks the start of the next explosion method. This shows tracker-based fan-out rather than explicit radius gating.

methods_detailed.name: updateWeather
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method synchronizes rain and thunder state changes from server simulation to clients. It caches the old isRaining value in flag before calling super.updateWeather to advance strengths. If rainingStrength changed it sends S2BPacketChangeGameState reason 7 with the new strength to all players in the dimension. If thunderingStrength changed it sends reason 8 similarly dimension gated. These two paths handle gradual fade without a full rain toggle. If the boolean raining state flipped, it sends a global toggle to all players with reason 2 for stop or reason 1 for start. It then follows with global sends of reason 7 and reason 8 to resync strengths everywhere. The dimension-scoped sends use sendPacketToAllPlayersInDimension while toggles use sendPacketToAllPlayers. No distance radius like 64.0D or 512.0D is used because weather is global. This produces at most four packets per transition.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The flag save plus super call detects rain edges and strength deltas. The first two if blocks compare prev versus current strengths and send S2B reason 7 or 8 dimension gated. The outer flag comparison detects start versus stop transitions. The inner if sends reason 2 stop or reason 1 start globally. The final two sends rebroadcast strengths 7 and 8 globally after a toggle. This separates gradual strength sync from discrete rain state sync.

methods_detailed.name: spawnParticle(longDistance)
methods_detailed.detail_long: This overload is the core particle broadcast with explicit longDistance flag. It first builds a single S2APacketParticles instance reused for every recipient to save allocation. The packet packs particle type, longDistance flag, float position, float offsets, float speed, count, and varargs. It then loops over playerEntities in this dimension by index. For each EntityPlayerMP it gets the player BlockPos and computes distanceSq to the spawn coordinates. If that squared distance is at most 256.0D the player receives it, which equals 16 blocks normal view distance. Alternatively if longDistance is true and distance is at most 65536.0D the player receives it, which equals 256 blocks. The same Packet object is sent via playerNetServerHandler.sendPacket to each qualifier. No dimension helper is called because the list is already dimension scoped. This dual threshold lets command or beacon effects travel far while normal effects stay local.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature exposes particle type, longDistance, position, count, offsets, speed, and extra args. The packet construction line casts doubles to floats and reuses one instance. The loop resolves each player position and computes distanceSq. The if condition implements 256.0D short versus 65536.0D long gating. The sendPacket line delivers the shared instance only to qualifiers. This is per-player distance filtering without chunk map lookup.

methods_detailed.name: tick
methods_detailed.detail_long: This is the per-tick driver for the server world simulation and network flush. It first advances pending block ticks via tickUpdates and random block ticks via updateBlocks with no direct packets. It then enters the chunkMap section by calling thePlayerManager.updatePlayerInstances which flushes S21 S22 S23 block deltas to chunk watchers. Village ticking, siege ticking, and portal staleness removal run next without networking. The profiler sections wrap each subsystem for timing. At the very end it calls sendQueuedBlockEvents to fan out validated S24 block-action packets at 64.0D radius. This ordering ensures block state changes are sent before dependent block events in the same tick. If no players are present, updatePlayerInstances still runs but has no recipients. The method therefore indirectly causes all chunk block packets plus S24 each tick.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The tickPending plus tickUpdates lines advance scheduled block ticks. The chunkMap plus updatePlayerInstances line is the indirect S21 S22 S23 fan-out point. The village and portal lines run non-network simulation. The final sendQueuedBlockEvents line triggers S24 64.0D fan-out. Profiler markers show ordering but do not affect packets. This excerpt is the packet-relevant tail of the tick method.

methods_detailed.name: clickBlock
methods_detailed.detail_long: clickBlock first enforces adventure and spectator rules, returning false for spectators and for adventure players without allowEdit or whose held item cannot destroy the target block. It then enforces world border containment on the block position, refusing clicks outside the border. In creative mode it queues C07 START_DESTROY_BLOCK with position and face, calls clickBlockCreative for instant local break, and sets blockHitDelay to 5 to throttle repeats. In survival it aborts any prior target with C07 ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK to the old currentBlock when switching positions, then queues C07 START_DESTROY_BLOCK for the new location. It calls onBlockClicked for zero-damage starts, instantly breaks when relative hardness reaches 1.0, else initializes isHittingBlock, currentBlock, currentItemHittingBlock, curBlockDamageMP zero and crack overlay. The server validates reach, hardness and timing, so nuker cheats that spam START without STOP are detected here.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The border contains check runs before any packet, so out-of-border clicks never reach the server. The creative branch shows the START_DESTROY plus instant client break plus 5-tick delay pattern, explaining creative nuker speed limits. The survival branch first sends ABORT for the stale currentBlock when retargeting, keeping server crack state consistent. The final START_DESTROY carries the new loc and face the server validates for reach and hardness, and suppressing ABORT leaves ghost cracks server-side.

methods_detailed.name: onPlayerDamageBlock
methods_detailed.detail_long: onPlayerDamageBlock first calls syncCurrentPlayItem so any hotbar change emits C09 before mining packets, keeping server held-item in sync. It honors blockHitDelay by decrementing and returning true to swallow clicks during the 5-tick cooldown after place or break. In creative with border containment it re-sends C07 START_DESTROY_BLOCK and instantly breaks via clickBlockCreative, re-arming the delay. If isHittingPosition confirms the same block and held item, it returns false on air to clear isHittingBlock, else adds getPlayerRelativeBlockHardness to curBlockDamageMP for progressive cracking. Every 4 stepSoundTickCounter ticks it plays the block step sound locally at the block center for feedback. When curBlockDamageMP reaches 1.0 it clears isHittingBlock, sends C07 STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK, calls onPlayerDestroyBlock for local removal, zeroes damage and re-arms delay. Otherwise it falls through to clickBlock to start a new target, so holding mouse produces START, progress, STOP sequencing.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The hardness accumulation line advances crack progress per tick based on tool, haste and block strength, so speed-mine cheats inflate this value locally but the server recomputes it. The step-sound block plays every fourth tick purely client-side with no packet, giving audio feedback during digging. The 1.0 threshold branch sends STOP_DESTROY_BLOCK with exact pos and face, which is the only packet the server accepts as a legitimate break. sendBlockBreakProgress updates the local crack overlay from 0 to 9, and forging STOP without real progress is the core fast-break detection signal.

methods_detailed.name: onPlayerRightClick
methods_detailed.detail_long: onPlayerRightClick first syncs the hotbar via syncCurrentPlayItem so the server sees the correct held item for placement. It computes hitVec offsets f, f1, f2 as fractional positions inside the block for precise face placement and tile orientation. It rejects clicks outside the world border with no packet, preventing border-bypass builds. In non-spectator it tries onBlockActivated for doors, chests and levers when not sneaking with an item, setting flag true to indicate activation consumed the click. It validates ItemBlock.canPlaceBlockOnSide before sending, returning false early on illegal placement to save bandwidth. It always queues C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement with hitPos, face index, current item and f offsets, even for pure activation, because the server re-decides activation versus place. Locally it applies onItemUse with creative restore of damage and count versus survival consume, or returns true for pure activation. Spectators send C08 but skip local world changes, so the server must ignore their placements.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The onBlockActivated call predicts door or chest opening locally so the GUI feels instant, with flag recording whether activation succeeded. The canPlaceBlockOnSide check mirrors server placement rules for ItemBlock, aborting without a packet on illegal faces. The C08 line packs block position, face index, held stack and fractional hit offsets the server uses to orient slabs, stairs and pistons. Sending C08 even when flag is true lets the server confirm activation, and spamming C08 with crafted offsets is the scaffold and ghost-block vector.

methods_detailed.name: sendUseItem
methods_detailed.detail_long: sendUseItem blocks all use in SPECTATOR mode with an immediate false and no packet, enforcing spectator intangibility. It syncs the hotbar via syncCurrentPlayItem so the following C08 references the correct slot. It queues C08PacketPlayerBlockPlacement constructed from the current inventory item with the air-use constructor that uses -1 position internally. It records the pre-use stackSize, then calls useItemRightClick locally to predict food eating, bow drawing, potion throwing or snowball spawning. If the returned stack differs by identity or count it writes the result into mainInventory, clears to null on zero, and returns true to indicate consumption. If nothing changed it returns false, meaning the item had no right-click action. The server separately validates cooldowns, food hunger and projectile spawn on C08 receipt, so no-use-delay or fast-eat cheats forge timing around this packet.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The spectator early-return shows air-use is entirely disabled for that mode with no network traffic. syncCurrentPlayItem emits C09 first when needed so the C08 that follows is attributed to the right hotbar slot. The C08 air-use constructor signals right-click-air rather than block-place, which the server maps to food, bows and throwables. The stackSize comparison detects consumption locally for instant inventory feedback, while the server authoritative consume arrives later, so desync here causes ghost food or infinite snowballs if C08 is replayed.

methods_detailed.name: attackEntity/interactWithEntitySendPacket
methods_detailed.detail_long: attackEntity syncs the hotbar, queues C02PacketUseEntity with Action.ATTACK for the target entity ID, then applies attackTargetEntityWithCurrentItem locally only when not in spectator. interactWithEntitySendPacket syncs the hotbar, queues C02 with Action.INTERACT, and applies playerIn.interactWith locally only for non-spectators. isPlayerRightClickingOnEntity computes a hitVec offset from entity position, queues C02 with the Vec3 interact-at variant for armor stands and villagers, and applies interactAt locally for non-spectators. All three share netClientHandler as the sink and always send the C02 even in spectator, letting the server decide to ignore effects while still logging the attempt. The server validates distance, line of sight and cooldown, applying damage or leash or trade effects. Suppressing C02 creates silent aura where damage happens without animation, while spamming C02 with forged IDs is the reach and kill-aura vector. Local prediction keeps hits feeling instant pending S19, S0B or S06 confirmations.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: syncCurrentPlayItem before each C02 guarantees the server uses the current weapon for damage calculation rather than a stale slot. The ATTACK constructor carries only the entity ID, while the INTERACT and Vec3 variants add interaction coordinates for precise armor-stand handling. The spectator conditionals show packets are still sent but local effects are skipped, so the server is the final arbiter. Forging ATTACK with distant IDs is reach, and omitting the paired C0A swing is the no-swing signature.

methods_detailed.name: windowClick/sendEnchantPacket
methods_detailed.detail_long: windowClick obtains the next short transaction ID from openContainer.getNextTransactionID, applies slotClick locally for instant GUI movement with mouseButton and mode, then queues C0EPacketClickWindow with windowId, slotId, button, mode, resulting ItemStack and transaction ID. The server replays the click against its authoritative Container, validates the transaction, and corrects with S2F or S30 on mismatch. sendEnchantPacket queues C11PacketEnchantItem with windowID and button for the enchantment table selection, where the server rolls levels and applies S31 progress. sendSlotPacket and sendPacketDropItem queue C10 creative actions for set or drop slot, gated on isCreative to prevent survival item spawning. Racing C0E clicks against C0D close or spamming transaction IDs is the classic inventory-dupe and chest-stealer pattern. The local slotClick prediction is why containers feel instant despite round-trip validation.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: getNextTransactionID allocates the short the server will echo or reject in S32 confirm, linking each C0E to a server settlement. slotClick mutates the client Container immediately for responsive dragging, with the result stack echoed in the C0E for server comparison. The C0E constructor packs window, slot, button, mode and transaction together so the server can replay the exact click. The C11 line carries only window and enchant button, with the actual level cost decided server-side, so forged C11 buttons attempt free-enchant exploits.

methods_detailed.name: syncCurrentPlayItem
methods_detailed.detail_long: syncCurrentPlayItem reads the live hotbar index from mc.thePlayer.inventory.currentItem each call and compares it to the cached currentPlayerItem field. On mismatch it copies the new index into the cache and queues C09PacketHeldItemChange with that slot on netClientHandler. It is invoked at the top of updateController, click handling, damage, right-click, use-item, attack and interact paths, making it the universal pre-action hotbar sync. Because it only sends on change, scrolling without acting emits a single C09, while acting without scrolling emits none. The server applies the slot switch before processing the following C07, C08 or C02, so weapon or block identity is correct. Blocking C09 while switching items causes ghost-block or wrong-weapon hits where client and server disagree. The cache also drives isHittingPosition validation for mining continuity.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The inventory.currentItem read captures the live hotbar slot after number-key or wheel input. The inequality against currentPlayerItem filters redundant sends so idle ticks produce no C09. The C09 constructor carries just the slot index the server equips before handling the next action packet. If this sync is skipped the server applies C07 or C08 with the previous slot, which is the slot-desync behind far-place or wrong-tool anomalies.

methods_detailed.name: resetBlockRemoving/onStoppedUsingItem
methods_detailed.detail_long: resetBlockRemoving checks isHittingBlock and on true queues C07 ABORT_DESTROY_BLOCK with currentBlock and DOWN face, clears isHittingBlock and curBlockDamageMP, and clears the crack overlay via sendBlockBreakProgress with -1. It is called when the mouse is released, the target changes, or the held item switches via isHittingPosition mismatch. onStoppedUsingItem syncs the hotbar, queues C07 RELEASE_USE_ITEM with ORIGIN and DOWN placeholders, and calls stopUsingItem locally to end bow draw or food eat. Both use the C07 channel with distinct actions so the server can separate mining abort from use release. For bow release the server spawns the arrow based on draw duration, while for food it cancels eating progress. Omitting ABORT leaves server crack progress running, and omitting RELEASE allows fast-bow or no-slow exploits that the server times via packet intervals.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The isHittingBlock guard ensures ABORT is only sent when a dig was actually in progress, avoiding spurious server resets. The C07 ABORT carries the stale currentBlock so the server can clear crack state for that exact position. Clearing curBlockDamageMP and sending progress -1 removes the local crack overlay in step with the server. onStoppedUsingItem mirrors this with RELEASE_USE_ITEM for bows and food, so blocking either ABORT or RELEASE desyncs server progress timers used by anti-cheat.

methods_detailed.name: func_96536_a
methods_detailed.detail_long: This override broadcasts a score value change for a tracked objective. It first calls super to update the in-memory Score object. It then checks whether field_96553_b tracked set contains the score objective. Only tracked objectives produce network traffic, untracked ones stay local until burst. If tracked it calls sendPacketToAllPlayers with S3CPacketUpdateScore wrapping the Score. That fan-out has no distance or dimension gating and reaches every connected player. It finally calls markSaveDataDirty to persist the change via ScoreboardSaveData. This path handles score creation and value updates. Removal uses a different overload with name-only packet. The tracked set therefore filters global spam.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature takes the updated Score. The super call applies the local map change. The contains check gates networking on tracked status. The sendPacketToAllPlayers line builds S3CPacketUpdateScore from the Score. The markSaveDataDirty call flags persistence. This shows global ungated S3C fan-out for tracked scores.

methods_detailed.name: setObjectiveInDisplaySlot
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method synchronizes sidebar list and below-name display assignments. It caches the old slot objective then calls super to update the slot map. If the old objective differs and is non-null, it checks how many slots still reference it via func_96552_h. If still referenced elsewhere it sends S3DPacketDisplayScoreboard for that slot and new objective, otherwise it sends removal packets via sendDisplaySlotRemovalPackets. For the new objective, if non-null and already tracked it sends S3DPacketDisplayScoreboard globally. If new and untracked it calls func_96549_e to burst full state including S3B create, S3D slots, and S3C scores. It finally marks save data dirty. Slots 0 tab, 1 sidebar, and 2 below name map to the 19 internal slots. No radius or dimension gating applies.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature binds slot index and new objective. The cache plus super lines detect old versus new. The orphan check uses func_96552_h count to choose S3D update versus removal burst. The new objective branch sends S3D if tracked else bursts via func_96549_e. The S3DPacketDisplayScoreboard constructor packs slot and objective. The final dirty mark persists slot assignment.

methods_detailed.name: addPlayerToTeam
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method adds a member to a team and notifies all clients. It first calls super.addPlayerToTeam to update the membership map. If super returns false because the player is already on that team, it returns false with no packet. On success it resolves the ScorePlayerTeam via getTeam for the new team name. It then sends S3EPacketTeams globally via sendPacketToAllPlayers with team, singleton player list, and action 3 join. Action 3 means add players to existing team without resending full fields. The fan-out is global with no 16.0D or 64.0D radius and no dimension filter. It marks save data dirty for persistence and returns true. Clients then render nametag and friendly-fire rules accordingly.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature takes player name and team name. The super if gates networking on membership change. The getTeam line resolves the team object. The sendPacketToAllPlayers line builds S3EPacketTeams with action 3 and single-player list. The dirty mark plus true return confirms persistence. The else returns false with no broadcast. This is global S3E join fan-out.

methods_detailed.name: removePlayerFromTeam
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method removes a member from a team and broadcasts the leave. It first calls super.removePlayerFromTeam to update the server map, which throws if the player is not on that team. It then sends S3EPacketTeams globally with team, singleton list, and action 4 leave. Action 4 tells clients to drop that entry from the team roster. Delivery uses sendPacketToAllPlayers with no distance or dimension gating. It finally marks save data dirty for disk persistence. The packet carries only the affected player, not the full roster. If multiple leaves occur each generates its own packet with no batching. This keeps team rosters consistent for tab list and collisions.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment warns about IllegalStateException for non-members. The signature binds player name and team object. The super call mutates the roster or throws. The sendPacketToAllPlayers line builds S3EPacketTeams action 4 leave. The markSaveDataDirty call persists removal. This is global ungated single-player S3E update.

methods_detailed.name: broadcastTeamCreated
methods_detailed.detail_long: This callback registers a newly created team on all clients. It first calls super.broadcastTeamCreated to add the team to the server map. It then sends S3EPacketTeams with the team object and action 0 create via sendPacketToAllPlayers. Action 0 carries full team fields including display name, prefix, suffix, friendly fire, and visibility. The broadcast is global with no radius or dimension filtering. It marks save data dirty to persist the new team. The paired removal uses func_96513_c with action 1. Without this packet clients would not know the team exists for later join actions. Late joiners receive teams again via burst logic.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment states client registration intent. The signature takes the new ScorePlayerTeam. The super call stores it server side. The sendPacketToAllPlayers line builds S3EPacketTeams action 0 create. The dirty mark persists creation. This is global full-state S3E fan-out.

methods_detailed.name: sendTeamUpdate
methods_detailed.detail_long: This callback pushes team property edits to all clients. It first calls super.sendTeamUpdate to update the server team object. It then sends S3EPacketTeams with the team and action 2 update via sendPacketToAllPlayers. Action 2 carries prefix, suffix, friendly fire, see friendly invisibles, and name tag visibility changes. The fan-out is global with no distance or dimension gate. It marks save data dirty for persistence. Membership is unchanged, so no player list is included unlike actions 3 and 4. Clients apply the new display fields immediately to tab and overhead names. Frequent prefix changes each generate a packet without coalescing.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment identifies property update intent. The signature takes the edited team. The super call applies local fields. The sendPacketToAllPlayers line builds S3EPacketTeams action 2. The dirty mark persists the edit. This is global S3E property sync without roster payload.

methods_detailed.name: onObjectiveDisplayNameChanged
methods_detailed.detail_long: This callback renames a tracked objective on all clients. It first calls super.onObjectiveDisplayNameChanged to update the server display string. It then checks whether field_96553_b tracked set contains the objective. Only tracked objectives broadcast, untracked renames remain local until a later burst. If tracked it sends S3BPacketScoreboardObjective with the objective and action 2 update via sendPacketToAllPlayers. Action 2 means update display text without recreating scores. The send is global with no radius or dimension gating. It finally marks save data dirty. Clients update sidebar and tab headers on receipt. Creation uses action 0 and removal uses action 1 elsewhere.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature takes the renamed ScoreObjective. The super call updates the server name. The contains check filters to tracked objectives only. The sendPacketToAllPlayers line builds S3B action 2 rename. The dirty mark persists the new name. This shows conditional global S3B fan-out.

methods_detailed.name: func_96549_e
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method bursts full objective state to all players for late joiners or new objectives. It builds the packet list via func_96550_d, which creates S3BPacketScoreboardObjective action 0 create, plus S3DPacketDisplayScoreboard for each of 19 slots referencing it, plus S3CPacketUpdateScore per sorted score. It then loops over every EntityPlayerMP in the configuration manager player list. For each player it loops the list and sends each Packet via playerNetServerHandler.sendPacket. After the fan-out it adds the objective to field_96553_b tracked set so future deltas broadcast incrementally. Delivery is global with no distance or dimension gating. This is the heaviest scoreboard burst, proportional to score count. It pairs with sendDisplaySlotRemovalPackets for teardown.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature takes the new ScoreObjective to publish. The func_96550_d call builds S3B plus S3D plus S3C list. The outer loop visits every online player. The inner loop sends each packet in order via playerNetServerHandler. The add call marks the objective tracked. This is ordered global burst for synchronization.

methods_detailed.name: sendDisplaySlotRemovalPackets
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method removes an objective everywhere including display slots. It builds the removal list via func_96548_f, which creates S3BPacketScoreboardObjective action 1 remove plus S3DPacketDisplayScoreboard entries for each occupied slot among 19. It then loops over every EntityPlayerMP in the player list. For each player it sends every Packet in that list via playerNetServerHandler.sendPacket. After delivery it removes the objective from field_96553_b tracked set so future score edits stay local. The fan-out is global with no radius or dimension gating. Clients clear sidebar, list, and below-name displays referencing the objective. This is the symmetric teardown to func_96549_e burst creation.

methods_detailed.name: processLoginStart
methods_detailed.detail_long: processLoginStart handles C00 hello and branches online versus offline login. It validates state equals HELLO via Validate, throwing on duplicate hello. It stores the GameProfile from the packet. If online mode is enabled and the channel is not local, it moves to KEY state and sends S01 EncryptionRequest with empty serverId, server public key and four-byte verifyToken. Otherwise for offline or singleplayer it jumps directly to READY_TO_ACCEPT. No kick occurs here, errors throw IllegalStateException. The verifyToken nonce later proves the client holds the private key. Local channels skip encryption to reduce latency.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: Validate.validState enforces the HELLO to KEY to AUTH state machine and rejects replays. Storing loginGameProfile preserves the requested name for later Mojang verification. The online-mode plus not-local gate selects encrypted versus instant accept. S01PacketEncryptionRequest carries serverId, public key and verifyToken nonce. The else moves offline logins straight to READY_TO_ACCEPT for tryAcceptPlayer.

methods_detailed.name: processEncryptionResponse
methods_detailed.detail_long: processEncryptionResponse handles C01 key exchange in KEY state. It validates KEY state, fetches the server private key and compares the decrypted verifyToken with Arrays equals, throwing Invalid nonce on mismatch to block replay. On match it decrypts the shared secret, moves to AUTHENTICATING and enables encryption on the channel. It then spawns User Authenticator thread with incrementing ID to avoid blocking netty. That thread hashes serverId, public key and secret via CryptManager, calls hasJoinedServer to verify the Mojang session, and on success sets READY_TO_ACCEPT. Singleplayer fallback generates offline profiles when verification fails or auth servers are down, otherwise it closes with Failed to verify username. No S packets are sent here directly.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The KEY state check rejects out-of-order C01 packets. Decrypting verifyToken with the private key and comparing to stored nonce detects tampering. Throwing Invalid nonce aborts the login without a graceful S00. Storing secretKey, setting AUTHENTICATING and enabling encryption switch the channel to ciphered mode. Spawning the authenticator thread offloads the blocking Mojang HTTPS check.

methods_detailed.name: update
methods_detailed.detail_long: update ticks the login state machine and enforces the 600-tick timeout. If state is READY_TO_ACCEPT it calls tryAcceptPlayer immediately to apply bans and compression. If state is DELAY_ACCEPT it polls for the duplicate old player by UUID, and when null it flips to READY_TO_ACCEPT, initializes the new player and clears the pending reference. It increments connectionTimer every tick and closes with Took too long to log in via S00 Disconnect at exactly 600. DELAY_ACCEPT exists because createPlayerForUser kicks the old session but the logout needs ticks to complete. No PLAY packets are sent here, only login S00, S02 and S03 via helpers. Stuck AUTHENTICATING threads eventually hit the same timeout.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The READY_TO_ACCEPT branch drives immediate accept without waiting for network events. The DELAY_ACCEPT branch looks up the old UUID entry to detect when the kicked duplicate has logged out. Null means safe to initializeConnectionToPlayer with the staged player object. The connectionTimer post-increment equals 600 gate sends S00 Took too long to log in. That timeout bounds Mojang outages and stalled encryption handshakes.

methods_detailed.name: tryAcceptPlayer
methods_detailed.detail_long: tryAcceptPlayer applies final login gates and switches to PLAY. It completes incomplete profiles with getOfflineProfile deriving OfflinePlayer UUIDs. It calls allowUserToConnect and closes with the ban, whitelist, IP or full reason when non-null. On success it sets ACCEPTED, and if compression threshold is non-negative on a remote channel it sends S03 EnableCompression then sets the threshold on future. It sends S02 LoginSuccess with the verified profile to trigger client PLAY switch. It checks for duplicate UUID sessions, staging a new player and entering DELAY_ACCEPT when found, otherwise initializing immediately via createPlayerForUser. No teleport occurs, the follow-up initializeConnectionToPlayer sends the S01 burst. Offline servers always take the instant path.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: allowUserToConnect returns null only when bans, whitelist, IP and capacity all pass. Non-null triggers closeConnection with S00 carrying that reason. Setting ACCEPTED plus S03 EnableCompression negotiates compression before LoginSuccess. S02PacketLoginSuccess carries the final UUID and name to switch the client to PLAY. The UUID duplicate check stages DELAY_ACCEPT versus immediate initializeConnectionToPlayer for overlap handling.

methods_detailed.name: closeConnection
methods_detailed.detail_long: closeConnection terminates a login with S00 Disconnect and channel close. It logs the connection info plus reason for audit. It wraps the reason in ChatComponentText, sends S00PacketDisconnect, then closes the channel with the same component. Exceptions during send or close are caught and logged as Error whilst disconnecting player without rethrow. It is used for ban kicks, auth failures, duplicate handling and the 600-tick timeout. No PLAY packets are involved because the pipeline is still in LOGIN state. The client displays the text on the disconnected screen.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The try block ensures logging and packet send happen atomically. getConnectionInfo includes profile and remote address for forensics. S00PacketDisconnect carries the human-readable kick reason to the client. closeChannel with the same component tears down the netty pipeline. The catch prevents disconnect-path exceptions from crashing the server tick.

methods_detailed.name: getOfflineProfile
methods_detailed.detail_long: getOfflineProfile derives deterministic offline UUIDs for cracked and singleplayer logins. It concatenates OfflinePlayer colon plus original name, encodes as UTF-8 bytes and hashes with nameUUIDFromBytes version three. It returns a new GameProfile with that UUID and the original name preserving case. It is called by tryAcceptPlayer for incomplete profiles and by the auth thread when Mojang verification fails on singleplayer or auth servers are down. Online verified logins never use this path. No packets are sent here, the UUID feeds allowUserToConnect and S02 LoginSuccess. The deterministic mapping lets offline servers keep consistent inventories by name.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The OfflinePlayer prefix plus name string is the canonical offline seed. getBytes with UTF_8 ensures cross-platform UUID stability. nameUUIDFromBytes produces a version-three UUID from that seed. Returning a GameProfile with that UUID and original name lets bans and NBT key by stable id. The following LoginState enum defines HELLO, KEY and later states for the handshake.

methods_detailed.detail_long: This IWorldAccess hook broadcasts a named sound to nearby players in the same dimension. It is called by world simulation when a block or entity emits a sound. It resolves recipients via ServerConfigurationManager.sendToAllNear at the exact x y z origin. The radius rule is volume scaled: 16.0D by default, or 16.0F times volume when volume exceeds 1.0F. This lets loud sounds like explosions or withers travel farther than quiet clicks. Dimension gating uses theWorldServer.provider.getDimensionId so nether and overworld do not cross hear. The packet is S29PacketSoundEffect built from sound name, position, volume, and pitch. No exclusion applies, so even the causing player hears it. When volume is above 1.0F the radius becomes 16.0F times volume, otherwise fixed 16.0D. Recipients are resolved with sendToAllNearExcept passing the except EntityPlayer reference. Dimension gating again uses theWorldServer dimension ID to prevent cross-dimension hearing. The packet is S29PacketSoundEffect with identical sound name, x y z, volume, and pitch fields. This is used for player-caused sounds where the actor plays the sound locally or should not double hear. All other nearby players in range still receive it. The only difference from playSound is the exclusion filter.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The comment states the except-player behavior. The signature adds the except EntityPlayer first arg. The body mirrors playSound but calls sendToAllNearExcept. The ternary preserves 16.0D versus 16.0F times volume scaling. The S29PacketSoundEffect args are unchanged. This shows exclusion plus dimension-gated radius filtering.

methods_detailed.name: playAuxSFX
methods_detailed.detail_long: This hook broadcasts a block auxiliary effect such as dispenser click or record break near a position. It excludes the triggering EntityPlayer passed in, so that player does not get a duplicate local effect. Recipients are resolved via sendToAllNearExcept with the block position coordinates. The radius is fixed at 64.0D regardless of volume, wider than the 16.0D base sound radius. Dimension gating uses theWorldServer dimension ID. The packet is S28PacketEffect constructed with sfxType, BlockPos, data, and false for non-global flag. The data field carries block ID or extra info depending on sfxType. This contrasts with broadcastSound which is global with true flag. Only players within 64 blocks in the same dimension receive it.

methods_detailed.name: broadcastSound

It calls sendPacketToAllPlayers directly so all dimensions hear it unless client filters. The packet is S28PacketEffect built from soundID, BlockPos, data, and true for global flag. The true flag distinguishes it from playAuxSFX ranged effects. Typical uses are wither spawn, ender dragon death, or portal events that need world-wide awareness. Because there is no dimension gating, overworld players can receive nether-originated global events. No exclusion applies, so the trigger player also receives it. This is the loudest scope in WorldManager.

The S28PacketEffect constructor uses true to mark global broadcast. The following lines reveal the start of sendBlockBreakProgress loop. This contrast shows global versus ranged S28 usage. For each candidate it first checks worldObj identity equals theWorldServer to enforce dimension separation. It then skips the breaker entity ID itself so the miner does not receive their own crack echo. It computes dx dy dz from block pos to player posX posY posZ. It checks squared distance less than 1024.0D which equals 32 blocks. Only qualifiers get a direct S25PacketBlockBreakAnim via playerNetServerHandler.sendPacket. The packet carries breakerId, BlockPos, and progress 0 to 9 or negative to clear. Each progress change sends a fresh packet with no batching. This tight 32 block scope keeps digging visuals local.

The dx dy dz lines compute offset for squared distance. The less than 1024.0D check gates to 32 blocks. The sendPacket line builds S25PacketBlockBreakAnim with ID, pos, and progress. methods_detailed.name: markBlockForUpdate
methods_detailed.detail_long: This is the server hook that queues a block change for chunk-scoped delivery. On the client the sibling does render updates, but on the server it only flags the chunk. It delegates to theWorldServer.getPlayerManager with markBlockForUpdate and BlockPos. No packet is constructed or sent immediately here. PlayerManager maps the position to chunk XZ via right shift 4 and finds the PlayerInstance. That instance records local coordinates and defers the packet choice to onUpdate next tick. A single flagged block later becomes S23, two to sixty three become S22, and sixty four trigger S21 full chunk. Only players watching that chunk receive the eventual flush. No packet is sent synchronously inside this method, so no radius like 512.0D applies yet. Viewer assignment uses tracking ranges configured per entity class. This is the entry point that eventually leads to spawn packet fan-out. Without this call clients would never learn about the entity. It complements onEntityRemoved which tears down tracking.

methods_detailed.detail_long: This method maps a world BlockPos to its chunk watcher and queues a delta. It derives chunk X and Z by arithmetic right shift 4 on block X and Z. If count equals one it decodes the single packed short into world x y z and sends S23PacketBlockChange to chunk watchers. It also sends the tile entity description packet if that block has a tile entity. If count equals sixty four it sends S21PacketChunkData with flagsYAreasToUpdate mask for full chunk resend plus tile entities per dirty section. Otherwise for two to sixty three it sends S22PacketMultiBlockChange with count, short array, and chunk reference plus per-block tile packets. For each EntityPlayerMP it checks whether loadedChunks contains the chunkCoords. If the player already fully loaded the chunk via the load queue, the packet is skipped to avoid duplicate S21 or delta spam. Otherwise it sends the supplied Packet directly via playerNetServerHandler.sendPacket. No distance math with 16.0D or 1024.0D is performed because subscription implies proximity. For each coordinate it fetches the PlayerInstance without creation. If non-null it calls removePlayer on the instance to drop the player from watchers and loadedChunks. methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature takes the mounted EntityPlayerMP. The chunk and delta lines compute movement squared. The greater than equals 64.0D gate equals 8 blocks before work. The j1 k1 check ensures a chunk boundary crossed. The nested loops add new watchers and remove stale ones via overlaps tests. Later lines reorder load queue and snap managedPos. This is differential S21 subscription update.

methods_detailed.name: filterChunkLoadQueue
methods_detailed.detail_long: This method reorders a player pending chunk load queue into spiral priority around the player. It copies loadedChunks to a temp list then clears the live queue. It computes view radius, central chunk XZ, and fetches the center PlayerInstance chunkCoords. If the old list contained the center it is added first for immediate S21 send. It then walks outward rings using xzDirectionsConst east south west north vectors with expanding step counts up to twice radius. Each visited coordinate is resolved to its PlayerInstance chunkCoords and re-added if previously queued. A final straight tail fills remaining edge chunks. This ordering makes closest chunks load first on login or teleport. The S21 chunk data sends later follow this queue order. No packets are built here, only queue order.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The signature takes the player whose queue is rebuilt. The copy plus clear lines snapshot and reset pending chunks. The center fetch plus contains check prioritizes the standing chunk. The nested k1 l1 loops walk the xzDirectionsConst spiral outward. Each step resolves chunkCoords and re-adds if previously pending. This controls S21 send order without sending directly.

methods_detailed.name: swingItem
methods_detailed.detail_long: swingItem starts a client-visible arm swing on the server and broadcasts it to all tracking clients. It first checks isSwingInProgress and swingProgressInt against half of getArmSwingAnimationEnd to avoid restarting a swing mid-stroke unless expired or invalid. On start it sets swingProgressInt to -1 and isSwingInProgress to true so updateArmSwingProgress will advance it next tick. It then guards with worldObj instanceof WorldServer to ensure this only runs on the logical server. It obtains the EntityTracker from WorldServer and calls sendToAllTrackingEntity with new S0BPacketAnimation(this, 0) where type 0 means swing arm. Receivers including the attacker itself if tracked and nearby players get S0B and play the swing animation without changing inventory or health. This keeps swings visual-only while combat damage is handled separately by attack logic. No DataWatcher change is made here because animation is transient.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The guard condition prevents overlapping swings by allowing restart only when idle, past half duration, or with invalid counter. Resetting swingProgressInt to -1 and setting isSwingInProgress starts the animation timer consumed by updateArmSwingProgress. The instanceof WorldServer check confines packet sending to the logical server and avoids client double-send. sendToAllTrackingEntity forwards the new S0BPacketAnimation with entity ID and type 0 to every tracking client. Clients then render the arm swing while server logic continues independently.

methods_detailed.name: onItemPickup
methods_detailed.detail_long: onItemPickup broadcasts the pickup beam animation when a living entity collects an item, arrow, or XP orb. It first rejects dead pickup entities with isDead and rejects client worlds with worldObj.isRemote so only the server emits packets. It fetches EntityTracker from the WorldServer to find all clients tracking the picked-up entity. For EntityItem it sends S0DPacketCollectItem with args picked-up entity ID and collector entity ID so clients can fly the item to the collector. It repeats the same S0D send for EntityArrow and for EntityXPOrb using identical constructor arguments. Receivers hide or remove the ground entity and render it moving into the collector inventory or body. No inventory mutation happens here; actual stack transfer is done by caller logic before or after this visual. This separation keeps visuals in sync even if stack handling differs by subclass.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The method signature takes the picked-up entity and stack size though size is unused for the packet. The isDead plus isRemote guard ensures only live server-side pickups broadcast. Getting EntityTracker from WorldServer provides the audience of tracking clients. Each instanceof branch constructs S0DPacketCollectItem with collected ID first and collector ID second. Tracking clients receive S0D and animate the orb, arrow, or item flying to the collector.

methods_detailed.name: onUpdate
methods_detailed.detail_long: onUpdate runs every tick to decay stuck arrows and sync changed equipment to tracking clients. It calls super.onUpdate first for base entity movement and then gates server-only work with !worldObj.isRemote. It reads arrow count from DataWatcher slot 9 via getArrowCountInEntity and if above zero initializes arrowHitTimer to 20 times 30 minus count. It decrements arrowHitTimer each tick and calls setArrowCountInEntity with count minus one when it expires, which updates DataWatcher slot 9 for S1C metadata sync. It then loops slots 0 to 4 comparing previousEquipment cache to getEquipmentInSlot current value with ItemStack.areItemStacksEqual. On mismatch it sends S04PacketEntityEquipment with args entity ID, slot index j, and new ItemStack so clients update rendered held item and armor. It also removes old attribute modifiers and applies new ones to attributeMap to keep damage, armor, and speed correct. It caches a copy of the new stack in previousEquipment to avoid resending every tick. Every 20 ticks it resets CombatTracker to age out old damage entries.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The !isRemote branch confines arrow decay and equipment broadcast to the server. Arrow logic reads DataWatcher slot 9 and uses arrowHitTimer as a countdown scaled by remaining arrows before decrementing the visible count. The for loop over five slots diffs cached previousEquipment against live getEquipmentInSlot. On inequality it calls sendToAllTrackingEntity with S04PacketEntityEquipment carrying entity ID, slot, and new stack. Receivers update the rendered equipment slot while the server also swaps attribute modifiers locally.

methods_detailed.name: attackEntityFrom
methods_detailed.detail_long: attackEntityFrom is the server damage pipeline that validates, reduces, applies damage, and broadcasts hurt state. Earlier guards reject invulnerable sources, client worlds, dead entities, and fire damage with fire resistance. Armor, absorption, and potion reductions are applied inside damageEntity before health in DataWatcher slot 6 is lowered. Revenge target, recentlyHit timer, and attackingPlayer fields are set from source.getEntity for loot and AI. If flag remains true meaning full hurt rather than throttled repeat hit, it calls worldObj.setEntityState with byte 2. WorldServer forwards that state as S19PacketEntityStatus with entity ID and op code 2 to all tracking clients. Receivers invoke handleStatusUpdate byte 2 to play hurt sound, set hurtTime to 10, and flash red. Knockback via knockBack and hurt or death sounds follow, with onDeath called if health falls to zero. Throttled hits skip the S19 broadcast and knockback by clearing flag.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The if flag block runs only for full-strength hits that should be visible and knock back. setEntityState with byte 2 is the packet trigger that WorldServer turns into S19 to tracking clients. setBeenAttacked marks velocityChanged except for drown so motion syncs. The entity-null check computes knockback direction from attacker position with a small random fallback to avoid divide by zero. knockBack then applies motion while attackedAtYaw orients the hurt tilt on receivers.

methods_detailed.name: onDeath
methods_detailed.detail_long: onDeath awards score, drops loot on the server, and broadcasts the death animation. It resolves the killer via getAttackingEntity and source.getEntity, then calls addToPlayerScore if scoreValue is non-negative. It notifies the killer with onKillEntity for achievements and AI. It sets dead to true and resets CombatTracker to close the combat log. Guarded by !worldObj.isRemote it computes looting level from the killer, checks canDropLoot and doMobLoot gamerule, then calls dropFewItems, dropEquipment, and rarely addRandomDrop. These spawn EntityItem and EntityXPOrb which have their own spawn packets. Finally it calls worldObj.setEntityState with byte 3 which WorldServer forwards as S19PacketEntityStatus op 3. Tracking clients receive S19 and play death sound, rotate the corpse, and start the death timer.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: Setting dead and resetting CombatTracker marks the entity as finished on both sides. The !isRemote guard confines looting calculation and dropFewItems plus dropEquipment spawning to the server. Looting level comes from the killer player while doMobLoot and canDropLoot gate drops. The final setEntityState with byte 3 always runs so WorldServer can broadcast S19 death. Clients then run handleStatusUpdate byte 3 to set health zero and invoke onDeath locally.

methods_detailed.name: handleStatusUpdate
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleStatusUpdate runs on the client to mirror hurt and death states received as S19PacketEntityStatus. For id 2 it sets limbSwingAmount to 1.5, copies maxHurtResistantTime into hurtResistantTime, and sets hurtTime and maxHurtTime to 10 for the red flash duration. It zeroes attackedAtYaw, plays getHurtSound with randomized pitch, and calls attackEntityFrom with generic zero damage to trigger hurt hooks without changing health. For id 3 it plays getDeathSound with randomized pitch, forces DataWatcher health to zero via setHealth, and calls onDeath with generic source to start client death animation. Both branches rely on the server having sent S19 op 2 from attackEntityFrom or op 3 from onDeath via setEntityState. Unknown IDs delegate to super.handleStatusUpdate for base entity handling like spawn particles. This keeps client visuals driven entirely by server broadcasts rather than local simulation.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The id 2 branch reconstructs hurt visuals by setting swing, resistance, and hurt timers plus sound. Calling attackEntityFrom with zero generic damage fires client hooks while early isRemote return prevents health change. The id 3 branch plays death sound, zeroes DataWatcher health, and invokes onDeath for corpse animation. Both branches are entered only when S19PacketEntityStatus with matching op arrives. Other IDs fall through to Entity super handler.

methods_detailed.name: addPotionEffect
methods_detailed.detail_long: addPotionEffect adds or combines a potion effect and schedules a metadata sync. It first calls isPotionApplicable which rejects regeneration and poison on undead creatures but allows all else. If activePotionsMap already contains the potion ID it calls combine on the existing PotionEffect to merge duration and amplifier, then calls onChangedPotionEffect with reapply true to refresh attribute modifiers. If new it inserts the effect into activePotionsMap and calls onNewPotionEffect to apply attribute modifiers to attributeMap. Both paths set potionsNeedUpdate to true so updatePotionEffects will recompute DataWatcher slots 7 potion color and 8 ambient flag. Those DataWatcher changes are sent by EntityTracker as S1C reflect S1CPacketEntityMetadata to tracking clients. Clients then render particles, tint, and invisibility without receiving a dedicated potion packet. Duration refresh packets at 600-tick intervals also flow through this dirty path.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The isPotionApplicable guard filters invalid undead heals and poisons before mutation. The containsKey branch merges into the existing effect and calls onChangedPotionEffect to reapply speed, damage, or health modifiers. The else branch inserts the new mapping and calls onNewPotionEffect to apply modifiers once. Both set potionsNeedUpdate so the next tick pushes DataWatcher slots 7 and 8 via S1C metadata.

methods_detailed.name: removePotionEffect
methods_detailed.detail_long: removePotionEffect removes a server-side potion and triggers attribute cleanup and resync. It removes the entry from activePotionsMap by integer potion ID and captures the old PotionEffect. If non-null it calls onFinishedPotionEffect which sets potionsNeedUpdate true and on the server removes attribute modifiers from attributeMap via Potion.potionTypes. The dirty flag causes updatePotionEffects to call updatePotionMetadata next tick, recomputing liquid color and ambient flag or clearing slots 7 and 8 if empty. EntityTracker then sends the changed DataWatcher entries as S1C S1CPacketEntityMetadata to all tracking clients. Receivers stop rendering that effect tint and particles and update invisibility. This differs from removePotionEffectClient which only edits the client map without attribute work. If the ID was absent no packet or modifier change occurs.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The map remove by boxed potion ID both unregisters the effect and returns it for cleanup. The null check avoids dirtying metadata when nothing was active. onFinishedPotionEffect sets potionsNeedUpdate and strips server attribute modifiers. The next server tick then emits S1C metadata with updated color, ambient, and invisibility flags.

methods_detailed.name: updatePotionMetadata
methods_detailed.detail_long: updatePotionMetadata recomputes potion-driven DataWatcher state for S1C sync. If activePotionsMap is empty it calls resetPotionEffectMetadata which writes 0 to slot 7 color and 0 to slot 8 ambient, then calls setInvisible false to clear invisibility. If non-empty it calls PotionHelper.calcPotionLiquidColor over all active effects to blend the particle tint integer. It writes slot 8 with 1 if PotionHelper.getAreAmbient returns true else 0 to control ambient versus strong particles. It writes slot 7 with the blended color integer for client spell particles. It calls setInvisible based on isPotionActive for invisibility ID so armor and body render correctly. EntityTracker detects these DataWatcher changes and sends S1C S1CPacketEntityMetadata to tracking clients. Clients read slots 7, 8, and invisibility flag to render potion visuals.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The isEmpty branch clears color and ambient slots and disables invisibility for the clean state. The else branch blends active effects into a single RGB integer and writes ambient flag to slot 8. Writing slot 7 publishes the tint while setInvisible mirrors the invisibility potion. Changed DataWatcher objects are then broadcast as S1C metadata to trackers.

methods_detailed.name: markPotionsDirty
methods_detailed.detail_long: markPotionsDirty flags potion metadata for refresh on the next tick. It sets the private boolean potionsNeedUpdate to true without touching activePotionsMap or DataWatcher immediately. The flag is consumed in updatePotionEffects which on the server calls updatePotionMetadata to rewrite slots 7 and 8 and invisibility. Those DataWatcher deltas are then sent by EntityTracker as S1C S1CPacketEntityMetadata to tracking clients. It is called by onNewPotionEffect, onChangedPotionEffect, and onFinishedPotionEffect after attribute modifiers change. This batches multiple adds or removes in one tick into a single metadata packet. If called on the client it only affects local particle spawning logic. No packet is sent synchronously inside this method itself.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The empty sendEndCombat stub shows combat packets are unused in this version. markPotionsDirty simply sets potionsNeedUpdate to true to defer work. The next updatePotionEffects tick sees the flag and calls updatePotionMetadata on the server. Resulting DataWatcher slot 7 and 8 edits flow as S1C metadata to tracking clients.

methods_detailed.name: ping
methods_detailed.detail_long: ping starts a modern STATUS ping from the multiplayer list against a ServerData entry. It resolves ServerAddress from serverIP, creates a NetworkManager with createNetworkManagerAndConnect, and adds it to pingDestinations for ticking. It initializes serverMOTD to Pinging, pingToServer to -1, and playerList to null as pending state. It installs an anonymous INetHandlerStatusClient whose handleServerInfo parses S00, handlePong computes latency, and onDisconnect triggers legacy fallback. After installing the handler it sends C00Handshake with protocol 47, host, port, and STATUS next state to switch the channel from HANDSHAKE to STATUS. It then sends C00PacketServerQuery to request ServerStatusResponse. The server replies with S00PacketServerInfo followed by S01PacketPong echo after the client C01PacketPing. Failures are logged without crashing the list thread.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The try block sends the two-packet STATUS opening sequence on the fresh NetworkManager. C00Handshake carries protocol 47 plus host and port and requests STATUS state. C00PacketServerQuery then asks for MOTD, version, players, and favicon. Throwables are logged so a bad address does not break the server list. Replies arrive as S00 and S01 handled by the anonymous handler.

methods_detailed.name: handleServerInfo
methods_detailed.detail_long: handleServerInfo handles incoming S00PacketServerInfo and prepares the latency probe. It first rejects duplicate S00 with a Received unrequested status close to avoid double parsing. On first reply it marks field_183009_e true and extracts ServerStatusResponse via getResponse. It copies MOTD formatted text into serverMOTD, protocol name and number into gameVersion and version, and online versus max counts into populationInfo with gray formatting. It builds playerList tooltip from GameProfile names plus an and N more suffix when sampled players are fewer than online count. It validates favicon prefix data:image/png;base64 before storing base64 icon data else logs invalid icon. It records field_175092_e with Minecraft.getSystemTime and sends C01PacketPing with that timestamp. The server will echo it in S01PacketPong so handlePong can compute pingToServer. It sets field_147403_d true to suppress legacy fallback.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The favicon branch validates the data URL prefix before caching icon bytes else logs an error. Clearing icon to null when absent removes stale images from the list. Recording system time in field_175092_e provides the latency baseline. Sending C01PacketPing with that value asks the server for an S01 echo. Setting field_147403_d marks the query complete to block compatibility ping.

methods_detailed.name: handlePong
methods_detailed.detail_long: handlePong handles incoming S01PacketPong and finalizes latency measurement. It reads the stored send time field_175092_e set when C01PacketPing was sent from handleServerInfo. It reads current time via Minecraft.getSystemTime as the receive time. It subtracts send from receive into server.pingToServer in milliseconds for the list display. It then closes the channel with Finished message to terminate the STATUS session cleanly. The outer pingPendingNetworks loop will later remove the closed NetworkManager and call checkDisconnected. No further packets are sent on this connection after close. Duplicate pongs are unlikely because the server closes after one S01.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The handler ignores packetIn time and uses the stored send timestamp for consistency. Getting system time at receipt captures round-trip delay including server processing. Assigning j minus i to pingToServer updates the list column. Closing with Finished ends the STATUS connection so resources are freed.

methods_detailed.name: onDisconnect
methods_detailed.detail_long: onDisconnect runs when the STATUS channel closes and decides whether to try legacy ping. It checks field_147403_d which is set true only after a valid S00 plus C01PacketPing sequence completed. If true it does nothing because modern ping succeeded even if the close reason is Finished or Cancelled. If false it logs Can't ping plus server IP and reason text via OldServerPinger logger. It sets serverMOTD to dark red Can't connect to server and clears populationInfo. It then calls tryCompatibilityPing on the outer OldServerPinger to attempt a pre-1.7 0xFE MC|PingHost exchange over raw Netty. That fallback can populate version, MOTD, and counts for old servers. Modern servers that refused the handshake will show the error text if legacy also fails.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The !field_147403_d guard distinguishes failed queries from normal Finished closes. Logging includes serverIP and disconnect text for diagnostics. Setting MOTD and populationInfo provides immediate list feedback. Delegating to tryCompatibilityPing opens a raw 0xFE channel for 1.6-era servers.

methods_detailed.name: tryCompatibilityPing
methods_detailed.detail_long: tryCompatibilityPing implements the legacy 1.6 Beta-style 0xFE server-list ping over raw Netty. It resolves ServerAddress and builds a Bootstrap on CLIENT_NIO_EVENTLOOP with NioSocketChannel and a ChannelInitializer. The initializer enables TCP_NODELAY and installs a SimpleChannelInboundHandler for ByteBuf. On channelActive it writes packet 0xFE, 1, 0xFA MC|PingHost with host string length, IP chars, and port integer, then flushes with CLOSE_ON_FAILURE. On channelRead0 it reads unsigned byte and expects 0xFF kick response, decodes UTF-16BE length-prefixed string, and splits on NUL with PING_RESPONSE_SPLITTER limit 6. If element zero equals section-1 it parses protocol, version, MOTD, online, and max with parseIntWithDefault into server fields. It then closes the context while exceptionCaught also closes on error. No modern C00 or S00 packets are used on this path.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: channelActive fires when the raw TCP connection opens before any STATUS handshake. Allocating an Unpooled buffer lets the code manually encode the 0xFE plus MC|PingHost payload. Writing 254, 1, 250 plus length-prefixed chars reproduces the Beta 1.8 ping format. Appending IP chars and port tells legacy servers which virtual host is queried. Flushing with CLOSE_ON_FAILURE sends the probe while cleaning up on write error.

methods_detailed.name: pingPendingNetworks
methods_detailed.detail_long: pingPendingNetworks pumps all outstanding server-list pings each client tick. It synchronizes on pingDestinations because ping and network threads can add or iterate concurrently. It obtains an iterator so closed channels can be removed safely during traversal. For each NetworkManager it checks isChannelOpen and if open calls processReceivedPackets to dispatch S00 to handleServerInfo and S01 to handlePong. If closed it removes the entry from the list and calls checkDisconnected to fire onDisconnect with the close reason. That disconnect step is what triggers legacy fallback when modern query never completed. It runs on the client thread from GuiMultiplayer update logic. Without this pump no STATUS replies would be processed.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: Synchronizing on pingDestinations prevents concurrent modification from ping creation. The iterator loop visits each pending NetworkManager once per tick. Open channels have processReceivedPackets decode and dispatch STATUS packets. Closed channels are removed and passed to checkDisconnected to deliver the disconnect reason. That callback completes latency display or legacy fallback.

methods_detailed.name: clearPendingNetworks
methods_detailed.detail_long: clearPendingNetworks cancels every outstanding server-list ping, typically when leaving multiplayer GUI. It synchronizes on pingDestinations for thread safety with concurrent ping adds. It iterates with an iterator to allow removal while traversing. For each NetworkManager it checks isChannelOpen and only acts on still-open connections. It removes the open entry from the list first to prevent pingPendingNetworks from processing it. It then calls closeChannel with Cancelled message to close TCP and fire onDisconnect. Already-closed entries are left for pingPendingNetworks cleanup rather than double-closed here. After return no modern STATUS or legacy 0xFE probes from this pinger remain active.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The synchronized block guards the shared ping list during cancellation. The iterator with isChannelOpen filter targets only live connections. Removing before close avoids race with the tick pump. Closing with Cancelled terminates handshake, query, or ping waits and releases Netty resources.

methods_detailed.name: NetHandlerStatusServer
methods_detailed.detail_long: NetHandlerStatusServer is the constructor that binds a STATUS connection to its server and channel. It stores the MinecraftServer reference used later to fetch cached ServerStatusResponse with MOTD, favicon, version, and player counts. It stores the NetworkManager used to send S00PacketServerInfo and S01PacketPong and to close the channel. It leaves handled false so the first C00PacketServerQuery will be accepted. The EXIT_MESSAGE constant Status request has been handled is shared for closes after query, duplicate query, or ping. No packets are sent inside the constructor itself. The handler lives only between handshake STATUS switch and login or disconnect.

Storing networkManager preserves the channel for sends and closes. Leaving handled false arms the one-shot query gate for processServerQuery.

methods_detailed.name: processServerQuery
methods_detailed.detail_long: processServerQuery handles incoming C00PacketServerQuery with a one-shot guard. If handled is already true it closes the channel with EXIT_MESSAGE to reject duplicate queries on the same STATUS connection. Otherwise it sets handled true to arm the guard before replying. It fetches the cached response via server.getServerStatusResponse containing description, players, version, and favicon. It constructs S00PacketServerInfo with that response and sends it via networkManager.sendPacket. The client OldServerPinger.handleServerInfo will parse it and follow with C01PacketPing. No channel close happens on the first query so the follow-up ping can arrive. A second query on the same connection is treated as abuse and disconnected.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The handled check enforces one query per STATUS session. Closing duplicates with EXIT_MESSAGE prevents info spam. Setting handled before send avoids race where a fast second query slips through. Sending S00PacketServerInfo with getServerStatusResponse delivers MOTD and counts. The channel stays open for the expected C01 ping.

methods_detailed.name: processPing
methods_detailed.detail_long: processPing handles incoming C01PacketPing and terminates the STATUS session. It reads client time via packetIn.getClientTime which is the timestamp the client sent in C01PacketPing. It constructs S01PacketPong with that same long value and sends it via networkManager.sendPacket. The client handlePong subtracts its stored send time from current time to compute pingToServer. Immediately after queuing S01 it closes the channel with EXIT_MESSAGE Status request has been handled. This enforces the query-then-ping-then-close sequence and frees the connection. No state validation on handled is done here because ping is valid even in edge orderings. Further packets on this channel will fail as closed.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The method extracts clientTime from the C01 request to echo it back. Sending S01PacketPong with that value lets the client match ping to send time. Closing with EXIT_MESSAGE ends the STATUS phase per protocol. The trailing brace closes the class after handling.

methods_detailed.name: onDisconnect
methods_detailed.detail_long: onDisconnect is the INetHandlerStatusServer disconnect hook for STATUS phase termination. It takes an IChatComponent reason describing normal Finished handling, duplicate query, or network error. Its body is intentionally empty because STATUS connections hold no player entity, inventory, or world state needing cleanup. Unlike play-phase handlers it does not broadcast quit messages or save data. The shared EXIT_MESSAGE close from processServerQuery and processPing flows through here as a no-op. Any resource release is handled by NetworkManager channel teardown itself. Leaving it empty also avoids touching MinecraftServer from the network thread on disconnect.
methods_detailed.code_walkthrough: The javadoc notes the reason parameter carries termination text. The empty body shows no player cleanup is required for stateless STATUS. The following processServerQuery header confirms disconnect needs no gate logic. NetworkManager handles socket close independently after this callback.
